articles.headline: Stephen Miller replaces Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff
articles.title: Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff after GOP’s midterm defeat
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced on November 6, 2026, that Stephen Miller is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff following the Republican midterm defeats. Wiles, the first woman in the post, is moving to the Trump Political Operation. Miller has been a close adviser and speechwriter since 2016.
articles.description: On his social media site, Donald Trump praised Susie Wiles and said she’d continue working for his political organisation

articles.headline: Donald Trump appoints Stephen Miller as new chief of staff
articles.title: Trump names Stephen Miller as new chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced that Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. Wiles resigned following Republican midterm losses. Democratic lawmakers criticized the appointment of Miller, who has been a key architect of administration immigration policies, amid expectations of congressional investigations starting in January.
articles.description: This is a breaking news story.

articles.headline: Global tech stocks tumble following U.S. midterm election results
articles.title: $2.5 trillion wiped off Nasdaq 100 as U.S. midterm outcome adds to AI stock slump
articles.summary: Global technology stocks slumped after United States midterm election results raised concerns over tighter regulatory scrutiny for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The Nasdaq-100 plunged 6.36% on November 5, 2026, erasing $2.53 trillion in market value. Semiconductor firms bore significant losses, though Indian equities bucked the trend with a strong rally as foreign investors bought shares.
articles.description: Democrats’ victories raise prospect of tighter scrutiny of data-centre projects as investors reassess AI spending; Indian equities buck global market weakness

articles.headline: Melania Trump hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials to discuss ceasefire
articles.title: Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials
articles.summary: US First Lady Melania Trump welcomed Russian and Ukrainian delegations to the White House to discuss a six-day ceasefire in the Kherson region. The truce allowed for the evacuation of residents from Oleshky. While officials praised the humanitarian progress, some analysts suggest the move was orchestrated by Vladimir Putin to influence US midterm elections.
articles.description: The US first lady was credited by all for playing a key though unspecified role in the ceasefire.

articles.headline: Melania Trump hosts Russia-Ukraine meeting after Oleshky ceasefire
articles.title: Melania Trump hosts Russia-Ukraine meeting after Oleshky ceasefire
articles.description: US First Lady Melania Trump has brought Russian and Ukrainian representatives together at the White House.

articles.headline: Iran reports multiple tanker fires in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says tankers struck in Hormuz amid fears of new US attack
articles.summary: Iranian forces reported that at least five oil tankers were damaged by naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the army stated the vessels caught fire while navigating the waterway. Separately, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported a tanker was struck by projectiles off the coast of Qatar.
articles.description: Iranian forces say five oil tankers and a tugboat have caught fire in several incidents in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns following bank collapse
articles.title: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
articles.summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigned after the collapse of Ueno Bank, a digital lender linked to his past business interests. The insolvency left millions of customers unable to access funds, triggering widespread protests and an impeachment push in Congress. Peña stated his departure aims to preserve social peace and democratic institutions within the country.
articles.description: The move follows a bank collapse and after the lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial against him.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules 24-hour magistrate production period begins from detention
articles.title: 24-hour arrest rule starts from detention: Supreme Court
articles.summary: On November 5, 2026, the Supreme Court of India ruled that the twenty-four hour timeline to present a detained individual before a Magistrate starts from the exact moment of detention rather than formal arrest. Justice Ujjal Bhuyan authored the judgment, stating that both actions restrict fundamental liberty and that Article twenty-two requires immediate release if the deadline is missed.
articles.description: The 24-hour rule to produce a detainee before court starts the moment a police officer ‘touches the body’ to restrain liberty, says top court; right to life and liberty cannot be curtailed by even ‘special statutes’ like UAPA, PMLA, NDPS, says court

articles.headline: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns amid banking crisis
articles.title: Paraguay President Pena resigns in wake of bank collapse
articles.summary: President Santiago Peña resigned on Thursday following the collapse of the digital lender Ueno, which left millions of customers without access to their accounts. Lawmakers had accused the president of conflicts of interest and negligence regarding the bank's insolvency. Vice President Pedro Alliana is expected to replace him as the impeachment process continues in Congress.
articles.description: President Pena, a Trump ally, had faced an impeachment motion and protests after the collapse of digital lender ueno.

articles.headline: Russell Brand convicted of rape and sexual assault in London court
articles.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault by UK court
articles.summary: A London jury at Southwark Crown Court convicted 51-year-old actor Russell Brand of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault on Thursday. Brand, who denied the allegations, was acquitted of other charges. Judge Joel Bennathan confirmed the defendant will be sentenced on Monday and faces a lengthy term in prison for his crimes.
articles.description: British comedian was convicted by jury at London court of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

articles.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football with Portugal
articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from the Portugal national team on Thursday after a 23-year career. The 41-year-old, who holds records for international appearances and goals, leaves following a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo, who remains active at club level with Al-Nassr, earned 234 caps and helped Portugal secure three major international trophies.
articles.description: The 41-year-old Portuguese legend says he will 'hand back the number 7 shirt' in social media post.

articles.headline: Voters and politicians push back against expansion of AI data centers
articles.title: All the latest updates on AI data centers
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence data centers face severe political and public backlash following the November 2026 midterms, where voters largely opposed expansion due to environmental and resource concerns. Tech companies are responding by promising greater community engagement and new energy commitments, while newly elected Democratic leaders demand stricter moratoriums and development restrictions.
articles.description: Massive new data centers are the physical foundation for tech companies’ hopes and dreams for AI. But the rush to expand warehouses full of energy-hungry servers has also kicked up fights across the world over their impact on power grids, utility bills, nearby communities, and the environment. Data centers were a major bipartisan issue ahead […]

articles.headline: Could Trump’s veto stop the Democratic majority?
articles.title: Could Trump’s veto stop the Democratic majority?
articles.description: Democrats have won the House and Senate. AJLabs looks at the numbers and what their majority means for Trump.

articles.headline: Sailor killed in Gulf missile attack as Iran reports burning tankers
articles.title: Sailor killed in Gulf as Iran says tankers on fire
articles.summary: A seafarer aboard the oil tanker Velos Sapphire was killed in a projectile attack in the Gulf on November 5, 2026, according to Velos Tankers. Simultaneously, Iranian state media and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reported that multiple tankers caught fire after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz following unauthorized transits.
articles.description: The Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Velos Sapphire was sailing to Bahrain empty of cargo when the attack happened on November 5, Velos Tankers said in a statement

articles.headline: Armed attackers kill thirty-three people in eastern DRC village raid
articles.title: Armed men kill at least 33 in village in Ebola-hit eastern DRC
articles.summary: Suspected Allied Democratic Forces militants raided Cantine village in North Kivu province, killing thirty-three people and burning over fifty houses. The assault forced patients, including individuals linked to an ongoing Ebola outbreak, to flee the local health facility. Local civil society leaders criticized the security forces for failing to prevent the violence.
articles.description: Locals blame ADF armed group, which pledged allegiance to ISIL in 2019, for the deadly raids on North Kivu villages.

articles.headline: Mohammed Shami retires from Test cricket after 12-year career
articles.title: Mohammed Shami retires from Test cricket, to continue playing white-ball formats
articles.summary: India pace bowler Mohammed Shami announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday through Instagram. The 36-year-old claimed 229 wickets in 64 matches since his 2013 debut. While injuries impacted his recent career, he will continue playing limited-overs formats for the national team. His memorable performances included key spells in South Africa during a distinguished career spanning over a decade.
articles.description: The 36-year-old claimed 229 wickets from 64 Test matches

articles.headline: U.S. Representative Ro Khanna criticises Hindu nationalism and supports student protests
articles.title: Condemn Hindu nationalism, support students’ protests: U.S. Representative Ro Khanna
articles.summary: United States Representative Ro Khanna condemned Hindu nationalism and supported Indian student protests on November 6, 2026, while speaking on digital platforms. The comments drew sharp criticism from senior Information and Broadcasting Ministry advisor Kanchan Gupta. Concurrently, the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom expressed concerns regarding alleged vigilante attacks on Gurdwaras in India.
articles.description: No response from MEA, but I&B Ministry advisor slams Mr. Khanna’s remarks; USCIRF claims shootings outside gurdwaras in Punjab are ‘vigilante attacks’

articles.headline: Russian battlefield gains slow down in Ukraine amid oil disputes
articles.title: Russia’s land gains in Ukraine dwindle as its diesel reportedly goes unsold
articles.summary: Russian military advances in Ukraine dropped significantly this year, with forces seizing 117.38 square kilometres in the first 10 months according to the Institute for the Study of War. Meanwhile, Ukraine targeted multiple Russian oil refineries to disrupt export revenues. Four tankers carrying diesel faced difficulties finding buyers due to the threat of United States sanctions.
articles.description: Moscow is suffering losses on the battlefield as US traders reportedly refuse to honour Trump's diesel deal with Putin.

articles.headline: Yemeni forces and Houthi rebels trade blame over Taiz market strikes
articles.title: Yemeni gov’t forces, Houthis trade blame for deadly strikes on Taiz market
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces and Houthi rebels exchanged accusations regarding a deadly attack on the al-Hadara market in the Taiz governorate. Houthi officials claimed Saudi-led air strikes killed 30 civilians, while military spokesmen stated the Houthi group fired ballistic missiles at the location. Ongoing fighting and a month-long siege continue to severely impact food and medicine supplies in the region.
articles.description: The attack on al-Hadara market in Taiz governorate's al-Waziiya district killed at least 30 people, Houthi rebels say.

articles.headline: Israeli opposition considers compromise on military conscription to form a new government
articles.title: Israel Opposition eases on ultra-Orthodox draft to oust Netanyahu
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Avigdor Liberman dropped demands for ultra-Orthodox military conscription on November 6, 2026, aiming to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Following the October 27 election, political factions face a divided landscape regarding coalitions and Arab-Israeli partnerships. President Isaac Herzog will announce the initial government-forming mandate on November 8, amid ongoing negotiations among multiple political parties.
articles.description: Listing the most important goals as removing Netanyahu and avoiding new elections, Opposition partner Avigdor Liberman said it was time to compromise and "understand that trying to have everything risks getting nothing".

articles.headline: Airstrikes on southwestern Yemen market kill at least 20
articles.title: Airstrikes on market in southwestern Yemen kill at least 30, Houthis say
articles.summary: Airstrikes in southwestern Yemen killed at least 20 people and wounded 15 others at a market in Taiz province on November 6, 2026. A Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson blamed the Saudi-led coalition for the attack. Local authorities in Taiz disputed responsibility, blaming the Houthi movement instead while confirming casualties occurred during the incident.
articles.description: A Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson, Anees Alsabahi, told Houthi-run TV Al Masirah that 15 people were also wounded in the airstrikes on the market in al-Waziyah in the province of Taiz

articles.headline: Jason Reding Quiñones resigns as U.S. attorney in Florida
articles.title: U.S. Attorney whose office oversaw Trump's election conspiracy probe resigns
articles.summary: United States Attorney Jason Reding Quiñones, whose office oversaw Donald Trump's election conspiracy probe, resigned on November 6, 2026. According to Attorney General Todd Blanche, the departure follows the Republicans' midterm losses. The Southern District of Florida office has been central to Trump's political investigations and transnational crime indictments, including that of former Cuban president Raul Castro.
articles.description: Jason ⁠Reding Quiñones’ resignation marked ⁠the departure of the second senior Justice Department official ​since the ‌Republicans devastating losses in the midterms

articles.headline: Paraguay Senate resumes impeachment proceedings against Santiago Pena
articles.title: Paraguay resumes Pena impeachment proceedings as financial crisis deepens
articles.summary: Lawmakers in Paraguay proceeded with impeachment actions against President Santiago Pena despite his resignation following a severe financial crisis. The Senate convened on Friday after the lower house overwhelmingly approved charges. The political turmoil erupted after the central bank intervened at Ueno Bank, leaving a significant portion of the population without access to public funds.
articles.description: Political turmoil comes after a digital bank's failure has left half the population without access to their accounts.

articles.headline: Two oil tankers catch fire in the Strait of Hormuz following mine collisions
articles.title: Iran Guards say two tankers caught fire in Hormuz
articles.summary: Two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after striking mines on November 6, 2026, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Iranian state media reported that the vessels were using unauthorised routes with United States military support. This event follows similar incidents reported on November 5 involving five tankers and a tugboat, though maritime officials have not confirmed the reports.
articles.description: Since the outbreak of the West Asia war on February 28, Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption

articles.headline: Trump discusses West Asia de-escalation with Qatari emir
articles.title: Trump discusses West Asia de-escalation with Qatar's Emir
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump spoke with Qatar Emir Sheik Tamim bin Hamad al Thani about regional de-escalation efforts amid tensions over potential military action against Iran. According to the Qatari media office, the leaders focused on diplomatic mediation to end the crisis, secure energy supplies, and protect maritime navigation across the region.
articles.description: The telephone call between Trump and Qatar's Emir Sheik Tamim bin Hamad al Thani centred on international efforts to end tensions, according to a statement from the Qatari ruler's media office

articles.headline: Trump administration postpones White House tech panel meeting
articles.title: Trump administration scraps meeting of panel that includes Meta's Zuckerberg, Nvidia's Huang
articles.summary: The United States administration postponed a scheduled meeting of the President Council of Advisers on Science and Technology. An Energy Department spokesperson confirmed the delay of the November 6, 2026 session, which includes executives like Meta Platforms Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg and Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, amid market turmoil.
articles.description: Technology shares sold ‌off ⁠dramatically on November 5 ⁠on growing concerns that a new Congress will slow AI development, and ​also on fears ‌that the massive capital expense of building out AI will not yield sufficient ‌returns

articles.headline: Millions of displaced Sudanese face shelter shortages amid severe funding cuts
articles.title: Millions fleeing Sudan’s war risk losing shelter as funds run low, UN warns
articles.summary: United Nations agencies warned on November 6, 2026, that millions of displaced people in Sudan risk losing emergency shelter due to severe funding shortages and empty warehouses. The ongoing civil war between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces has displaced 8.6 million internally. Humanitarian organisations currently lack the resources to assist more than ten percent of the 15.4 million vulnerable individuals.
articles.description: Fewer than 1 million of the 15.4 million people in need emergency shelter in Sudan have received assistance.

articles.headline: Militants kill at least 33 in eastern Congo village
articles.title: Islamic State-linked militants kill at least 33 in eastern Congo village attack, civil society says
articles.summary: Militants linked to the Islamic State killed at least 33 people in an overnight raid on Cantine village in eastern Congo on November 6, 2026. Local civil society leader Justin Paluku stated that over 50 homes were burned during the assault attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces, exacerbating security concerns amid an ongoing Ebola outbreak.
articles.description: The violence forced villagers to flee to other parts of the province, where the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak in history is raging

articles.headline: European troops prepare for possible post-ceasefire deployment to Ukraine
articles.title: European troops prepare for possible post-ceasefire deployment to Ukraine
articles.description: French- and British-led military drills in Poland will testing post-ceasefire deployment in Ukraine.

articles.headline: European Union says significant work remains to achieve Ukraine peace
articles.title: EU says 'a lot of work' still needed to reach Ukraine peace deal
articles.summary: The European Union announced that substantial effort is still required to secure a peace agreement in Ukraine, asserting that the bloc will independently manage its security affairs. This followed statements by United States President Donald Trump predicting a major deal involving Russia and all of Europe. EU spokeswoman Paula Pinho emphasized that willingness from the conflict initiator is necessary, while NATO and U.S. officials prepared for upcoming mediated talks in Abu Dhabi.
articles.description: Earlier, a NATO spokeswoman said Ukraine's allies are working for a "just and sustainable" end to the war ahead of U.S.-mediated talks next week in Abu Dhabi

articles.headline: Elon Musk reacts to Republican midterm election defeat on X
articles.title: U.S. midterm elections: Musk jokes about GOP election defeat after spending record sums on party
articles.summary: Technology billionaire Elon Musk posted a joke on the X platform on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, regarding the Republican Party defeat in the United States midterm elections. The comments followed his contribution of nearly five hundred million dollars to political efforts supporting Republican candidates in the race that saw Democrats seize control of Congress on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.
articles.description: Democrats seized control of the U.S. Congress on November 3, capturing both the Senate and House of Representatives

articles.headline: Democrats win key gubernatorial races across the United States
articles.title: U.S. Midterm election Democrats win five governor races as Hinojosa, Bottoms, Haaland make history
articles.summary: Democratic candidates secured major gubernatorial victories in Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Georgia, and Wisconsin during the elections held on November 4, 2026. Several contenders achieved historic milestones, including Keisha Lance Bottoms becoming Georgia's first Black female governor and Gina Hinojosa becoming Texas's first Latina governor. Voters focused heavily on the cost of living and President Donald Trump's unpopularity, according to U.S. media projections.
articles.description: Hinojosa becomes Texas’s first Latina governor, Bottoms the first Black woman elected governor in the US, and Haaland the first Native American woman to lead a state

articles.headline: Kenyan court sentences doomsday cult leader Paul Mackenzie
articles.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
articles.summary: Justice Diana Mochache handed down a 200-year prison sentence to Paul Mackenzie on November 6, 2026, following the deaths of 191 individuals in Shakahola forest. The leader of Good News International Ministries was found guilty of homicide and starvation-related offences after instructing followers to fast. Prosecutors had requested the death penalty, but the judge declined the punishment.
articles.description: Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could "meet Jesus".

articles.headline: Trump signals willingness to work with Democrats following midterm losses
articles.title: Veto or deals: Can Trump find a way to work with Democrats?
articles.summary: Following midterm elections where Democrats secured majorities in the House of Representatives and the Senate, United States President Donald Trump stated he would be willing to work with the opposition. According to University College London lecturer Andrew Proctor, the president faces legislative gridlock because Democrats lack a two-thirds majority to override vetoes. Meanwhile, newly elected Senator Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan expressed willingness to collaborate on key healthcare and foreign policy issues.
articles.description: Trump has three options to affect legislation, say analysts: veto legislation, enforce executive orders or make deals.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi drone over Medina region
articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says it downs Houthi drone over Medina; Houthis deny attack
articles.summary: Military forces aligned with the Yemeni government stated on November 6, 2026, that they shot down an explosive drone above the Saudi Arabian city of Medina. Representatives of the Houthi movement strongly rejected the accusation, maintaining that no military operations were directed toward the kingdom. The incident highlights escalating cross-border tensions linked to the broader conflict involving Iran.
articles.description: The Houthis have ​repeatedly denied targeting Mecca and Medina, Islam's ⁠two holiest cities, rejecting ⁠previous Saudi-led coalition accusations that it ‌had launched drones towards the cities

articles.headline: Zaporizhia aid strike death toll reaches fifty three amid ongoing rescue efforts
articles.title: Ukraine raises Zaporizhia aid strike death toll to at least 50
articles.summary: The death toll from a Russian aerial strike on an aid distribution centre in the Ukrainian village of Komyshuvakha rose to at least fifty-three after rescue workers recovered additional bodies from the rubble. Acting regional governor Mykhailo Semikin confirmed the figures as emergency services continued searches for missing individuals. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the double-tap attack on the shelter, while the United Nations human rights mission stated the incident likely violated international law.
articles.description: Ukrainian officials say DNA tests are being used to identify bodies while up to 39 remain trapped under rubble.

articles.headline: Intercity school bus crash in eastern France leaves two dead
articles.title: Bus carrying kids to school crashes in France, leaving 2 dead and 16 injured
articles.summary: French authorities reported that an intercity bus transporting students to educational institutions veered off the road and into a ditch on November 6, 2026, near Lent. The tragic incident resulted in two fatalities and injured sixteen other individuals, including three in critical condition. Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot and Education Minister Edouard Geffray expressed condolences to the affected families.
articles.description: News broadcaster BFM TV reported that the passengers included children travelling to middle and high schools in the area, with a photo from the scene showing the bus had veered off the road and landed in a ditch

articles.headline: Iran intensifies diplomatic outreach amid renewed United States military threats
articles.title: Russia to UAE, Iran steps up diplomacy amid Trump threats: What we know
articles.summary: Iran increased diplomatic efforts across the region after United States President Donald Trump suggested potential military action following drone incidents in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran presented a new nuclear and peace proposal through Qatari mediators, conditioned on the lifting of sanctions and unfreezing of assets. Concurrently, Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei traveled to Moscow to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss bilateral ties and economic cooperation.
articles.description: Iran launches diplomatic offensive as US mulls resumption of war.

articles.headline: Kenyan court sentences starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie to prison
articles.title: Kenyan court sentences starvation cult leader to 200 years
articles.summary: A Kenyan court sentenced starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie to two hundred years in prison for the murder of one hundred ninety children and one adult in the Shakahola Forest. Justice Diana Kavedza delivered the ruling on Friday, dividing the term equally between murder by starvation and direct homicide. Twenty-eight accomplices received various prison terms for their roles in the doomsday sect tragedies investigated by authorities since 2023.
articles.description: Paul Mackenzie and accomplices were convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult.

articles.headline: Indian stock markets rally as Sensex jumps 1,718 points
articles.title: Stock markets on fire; Sensex jumps 1,718 points, Nifty reclaims 25,000
articles.summary: Benchmark equity indices achieved a seventh consecutive daily advance on November 6, 2026, overcoming negative global market trends. The BSE Sensex rose by 1,718.01 points to close at 81,028.02, while the NSE Nifty surpassed the 25,000 threshold. Market analysts attributed the positive domestic sentiment to sustained foreign fund inflows and a decline in international crude oil prices.
articles.description: In the past seven consecutive sessions, the Sensex has surged 7,781.99 points, or 10.62%, and the Nifty rallied 2,331.5 points, or 10.27%

articles.headline: Air turns hazardous in New Delhi days before Diwali
articles.title: Air turns hazardous in New Delhi days before Diwali
articles.description: New Delhi’s air quality has turned hazardous days before Diwali, when celebrations often involve fireworks.

articles.headline: Why Abdul El-Sayed’s victory matters beyond Michigan | Explained
articles.title: Why Abdul El-Sayed’s victory matters beyond Michigan | Explained
articles.description: Abdul El-Sayed has made history by becoming the first Muslim elected to the United States Senate. The physician, epidemiologist and progressive Democrat defeated Republican Mike Rogers in one of the most closely watched races of the 2026 midterm elections. His victory comes despite record spending against his campaign and intense political attacks from opponents.

articles.headline: Russia reportedly supplies advanced missile launchers to Iran
articles.title: Rocket launcher deal illustrates deepening Russia-Iran relations
articles.summary: Moscow agreed to provide Tehran with ninety advanced missile launchers designed for attack helicopters under a 2024 accord, according to reports published on November 6, 2026. The revelation followed a Kremlin meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and senior Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei regarding bilateral security cooperation. Both nations continue to strengthen strategic ties despite heavy Western sanctions.
articles.description: Report of deal comes as top Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei discusses developing cooperation treaty with Putin.

articles.headline: Trinamool leader Abhishek Banerjee claims party lost assembly elections to Supreme Court
articles.title: We lost the elections to the Supreme Court, not to the BJP: Mamata-Trinamool’s Abhishek Banerjee
articles.summary: Diamond Harbour MP Abhishek Banerjee alleged on November 6, 2026, that his party lost the West Bengal Assembly elections to the Supreme Court rather than the Bharatiya Janata Party. The leader criticised electoral processes and Chief Electoral Officer Manoj Agarwal, while also addressing police custody cases and allegations surrounding recovered cash at a party office in his constituency.
articles.description: “Let the government of India or ECI take suo motu cognisance and file a case against me. I will represent myself and fight it at the Supreme Court,” Mr. Banerjee said.

articles.headline: Paraguayan President Santiago Pena resigns amid violent banking protests
articles.title: After Donald Trump’s midterm poll rout, South America breathes easy as far-right feels the heat
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of protesters flooded the streets of Asuncion on November 4, 2026, after being locked out of their accounts at the countrys largest bank, prompting President Santiago Pena to resign. As Congress moved to impeach him, Senator Antonio Velazquez stated on November 5 that Pena had disappeared and likely fled to Argentina to seek asylum following the unrest.
articles.description: Just a day after a blue wave swept across the U.S. in midterms election shaking President Donald Trump’s administration, the fall of Santiago Pena carries significance beyond the borders of the country of seven million people

articles.headline: Supreme Court settles decades-old energy dispute between Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, and Haryana
articles.title: Himachal to get 11,973 MU electricity from Punjab, Haryana as SC settles decades-old energy dispute
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India resolved a long-running dispute on November 6, 2026, directing Punjab and Haryana to supply 11,973 million units of electricity to Himachal Pradesh over 20 years. Led by Chief Justice Surya Kant, the bench enforced a cashless settlement based on a 2011 verdict regarding Bhakra Beas Management Board projects, ensuring historical construction costs were factored in without additional payments.
articles.description: SC said Punjab and Haryana will pay Himachal Pradesh 11,973 million units of electricity over a period of 20 years.

articles.headline: Global markets plunge as US tech stock rout spreads to Asia
articles.title: Tech stock rout, driven by US AI fears, continues in Asian trading
articles.summary: Asian trading faced severe disruptions on November 6, 2026, as a United States tech stock rout triggered market suspensions and sharp losses. Analysts attribute the downturn to fears that recent Democratic midterm victories will increase regulatory scrutiny on artificial intelligence infrastructure. Major indices including Japan's Nikkei dropped significantly while regional authorities intervened to stabilize local financial markets.
articles.description: Global markets are being roiled due to concerns over US data centre expansion and AI regulation.

articles.headline: Supreme Court identifies vehicular emissions as major contributor to Delhi air pollution
articles.title: Supreme Court terms vehicular emissions major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stated on November 6, 2026, that vehicular emissions heavily drive air pollution in the Delhi-National Capital Region as the air quality index approached the severe category at 391. During a hearing led by Chief Justice Surya Kant, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati outlined measures across five sectors, while the bench scheduled further review for November 16.
articles.description: The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi criticises Modi government over voter ID welfare scheme linkage proposal
articles.title: Not just vote theft, it's rights theft: Rahul Gandhi on Centre's 'Voter ID for welfare schemes' remark
articles.summary: Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi condemned government proposals on November 6, 2026, to replace Aadhaar with voter IDs for identifying welfare beneficiaries, calling the move a rights violation. Responding to remarks by Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Gandhi alleged that voter roll revisions are being used to manipulate electoral outcomes and restrict access to essential public schemes.
articles.description: Rahul Gandhi termed as a "conspiracy" the Modi Government Minister's announcement that benefits of schemes will now be determined not by Aadhaar, but by Voter ID

articles.headline: Ukraine raises death toll from Russian aid centre strike to 40
articles.title: Ukraine raises death toll from Russian strike on Zaporizhia to 40 people
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that the death toll from a Russian bomb attack on an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha rose to 40 people. The strike hit a school building and a shelter, killing four police officers and two rescue workers. The United Nations human rights mission stated the bombing likely violated international law as upcoming talks are scheduled in Abu Dhabi.
articles.description: Dozens may still be under the rubble in Komyshuvakha. Rescue efforts ongoing despite interruptions by Russian drones.

articles.headline: Somalia supreme court rejects president term extension amid growing political crisis
articles.title: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
articles.summary: Somalia's Supreme Court ruled that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud unlawfully extended his mandate, worsening a constitutional standoff following the disputed dismissal of Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed. The court ordered leaders to agree on an electoral plan within 30 days and hold elections within 90 days, challenging government timelines amid ongoing security threats from al-Shabaab militants across the country.
articles.description: The country's first nationwide elections since 1969 are due next year - a timetable now thrown into doubt.

articles.headline: Jharkhand High Court sets aside cancellation of JSSC-CGL exam
articles.title: Jharkhand HC quashes State Govt decision to cancel JSSC-CGL exam
articles.summary: On November 6, 2026, the Jharkhand High Court quashed the State government's decision to cancel the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission Combined Graduate Level exam and ordered the reinstatement of selected candidates with continuous service. The court stated the government failed to prove systemic irregularities, ruling that individual suspects should be investigated instead of terminating all appointments from the August 17, 2026 cancellation.
articles.description: The court has ordered the reinstatement of the candidates selected under advertisement number 10/2023, directing that their service be treated as continuous, without any interruption.

articles.headline: Devendra Nath Mahto launches yatra after Ranchi student protests
articles.title: Taking reforms to the road: From Ranchi protest to a Statewide yatra
articles.summary: On August 24, 2026, student leader Devendra Nath Mahto launched the Bharti Vyavastha Sudhar Yatra from Nemra village in Ramgarh district. Just six days after ending a 16-day hunger strike and student protests in Ranchi, the Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha leader began the second phase of his campaign demanding examination system reforms and government accountability.
articles.description: The students’ protest in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand’s recruitment exams for government jobs has remained in the news for most of August. Amit Bhelari examines the fallout of the government’s decision to cancel exams, which has left both aspiring candidates and already-appointed government employees caught in the dispute. It has pushed student leader Devendra Nath Mahto from a prolonged protest in Ranchi to a Statewide yatra demanding transparency, accountability and reforms in the government recruitment system

articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot secures majority recommendations to form new Israeli government
articles.title: Eisenkot tipped to seek Israel government with backing of Arab lists
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog will announce his decision on November 8, 2026, regarding who will form a new administration following the October 27 election. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot secured sixty-seven parliamentary recommendations compared to forty-six for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Two Arab-majority lists backed Eisenkot, while ultra-Orthodox party United Torah Judaism declined to make a recommendation.
articles.description: Isaac Herzog held a second day of consultations with political parties on November 5 after the October 27 election; he said he will announce on November 8 whom he will task with trying to form a new government

articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot emerges as favourite to form new Israeli government
articles.title: Eisenkot tipped to seek Israel government as religious party drops Netanyahu
articles.summary: Gadi Eisenkot emerged as the favourite to form an Israeli government on Thursday after President Isaac Herzog held consultations following the October 27 election. Neither Eisenkot nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a parliamentary majority. United Torah Judaism declined to recommend Netanyahu, while Arab-Israeli lawmaker Mansour Abbas recommended Eisenkot, who insists on closing military service exemptions for religious students.
articles.description: The Opposition leader also received a recommendation from a key lawmaker from the Israeli-Arab minority, whose seats in Parliament soared due to outrage over Netanyahu's policies

articles.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from Portuguese national team
articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from Portuguese national team
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo confirmed his retirement from international football on November 5, 2026, via social media. The 41-year-old forward stated he would relinquish the number seven shirt following the November international break. Ronaldo concludes his career with 234 appearances and 146 goals, holding the all-time records for both categories in international men's football history.
articles.description: Ronaldo has ‌made 234 appearances for Portugal and scored ‌146 goals

articles.headline: Nithya Raman defeats incumbent Karen Bass to become Los Angeles mayor
articles.title: India-born Nithya Raman beats Democratic incumbent to become LA mayor
articles.summary: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman won the mayoral election in Los Angeles, defeating incumbent Democrat Karen Bass after securing fifty-two percent of the vote. The India-born urban planner campaigned on affordability and neighborhood infrastructure improvements. Bass conceded the race on November 5, 2026, following the count in the nation's second-largest city.
articles.description: Leftist Nithya Raman, who was the first DSA-affiliated Los Angeles City Council member, will now helm the entertainment capital as it prepares to host the 2028 Olympics

articles.headline: Satellite images show new construction near Iranian missile sites
articles.title: Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest
articles.summary: Analysis of November satellite images by British intelligence company MAIAR indicates Iran is undertaking significant construction, repairs, and underground excavations at missile complexes and air bases like Garmdareh and Shahroud. Analysts suggest the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps is moving infrastructure underground to protect assets and rebuild military capabilities following repeated air strikes by the United States and Israel.
articles.description: Evidence of digging and new buildings are visible in satellite imagery taken in November, satellite images suggest.

articles.headline: Democrats win US Congress control in midterm election
articles.title: Making sense of the blue shift in U.S. midterm election | a collection
articles.summary: Democrats won control of the United States Senate and House of Representatives in the midterm election on November 3, 2026, dealing major defeats to President Donald Trump's Republican Party. In a national wave, Republicans lost gubernatorial and Senate seats in traditional strongholds like Texas, Georgia, and Ohio, with several historic victories achieved by Democratic candidates across the country.
articles.description: Analytical insights from The Hindu on the 2026 U.S. midterm results, blue wave shifts, and key state races

articles.headline: Global tech stocks plunge over fears of AI curbs in US
articles.title: Global tech stocks plunge over fears of AI curbs in US
articles.description: Asian markets plunged Friday, tracking a sell-off in Western stocks following the US midterm elections.

articles.headline: Israeli President Herzog to name government candidate on Sunday
articles.title: Israel’s President Herzog to name candidate to form government on Sunday
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced on Thursday that he will name a candidate to form the next government by Sunday after 67 lawmakers backed opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Following talks with the 120-seat parliament, Herzog faces the task of resolving political divisions as Eisenkot attempts to assemble a governing coalition amid disputed election integrity claims.
articles.description: Announcement comes after majority of Israeli lawmakers endorse Eisenkot over Netanyahu.

articles.headline: India's Maratha military landscapes added to UNESCO World Heritage List
articles.title: India's 'Maratha Military Landscapes' inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage List
articles.summary: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization inscribed twelve components of the Maratha Military Landscapes onto its World Heritage List during the forty-seventh session of the World Heritage Committee held in Paris. Developed between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries, these fortifications located in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu showcase the strategic military powers of the historic rule.
articles.description: Its 12 components are — Salher Fort, Shivneri Fort, Lohgad, Khanderi Fort, Raigad, Rajgad, Pratapgad, Suvarnadurg, Panhala Fort, Vijay Durg, and Sindhudurg in Maharashtra, and Gingee Fort in Tamil Nadu.

articles.headline: Macau sentences pro-democracy campaigner Au Kam San to twelve years
articles.title: Macau jails pro-democracy campaigner in city's first national security case
articles.summary: Au Kam San, a sixty-nine-year-old former lawmaker and pro-democracy campaigner in Macau, was sentenced to twelve years and six months in prison following a closed-door trial. Convicted of subversion against state power, his case marks the city's first national security trial. His wife condemned the ruling as groundless persecution, while authorities defended the proceedings as necessary for national security.
articles.description: Au Kam San was sentenced to 12 years and six months' jail for "subversion against the political power of the state".

articles.headline: Cancer patients in Karnataka face high treatment costs
articles.title: Cancer care: Long battle for affordable treatment
articles.summary: Two cancer patients in Karnataka face severe financial distress while undergoing expensive medical therapies. A garment worker from Bengaluru Rural diagnosed with mouth cancer requires funds for chemotherapy and surgery, while a shopkeeper from Mysuru needs costly immunotherapy for hypopharyngeal cancer. Both individuals struggle with treatment expenses that far exceed their modest monthly household incomes.
articles.description: Advances in oncology have improved treatment options, but their benefits remain out of reach for many patients who cannot afford to complete the prescribed course. This is despite the recent decision to cap trade margins on 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines, providing some relief, writes Afshan Yasmeen...

articles.headline: Donald Trump predicts major Russia deal involving Ukraine and Europe
articles.title: Donald Trump predicts deal with Russia on Ukraine and ‘all of Europe’
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump predicted a very large agreement with Russia involving the Ukraine war and all of Europe following an unscheduled meeting at the White House with Kirill Dmitriev. The Thursday encounter occurred while Russian and Ukrainian officials gathered for talks hosted by First Lady Melania Trump. The remarks raised European concerns regarding potential concessions to the Kremlin, although previous promises of rapid peace deals by the administration have failed to materialize.
articles.description: The U.S. president’s comments will fuel European fears that Mr. Trump is pivoting towards the Kremlin and will push Ukraine into an unfavorable deal to end Russia’s invasion

articles.headline: Key moments as Democrats sweep to victories in US midterms
articles.title: Key moments as Democrats sweep to victories in US midterms
articles.description: Democrats have been celebrating across the US after a series of victories saw them take control of both chambers.

articles.headline: Iran exempts select countries from Strait of Hormuz restrictions
articles.title: Why is Iran exempting India, China, Qatar, Iraq from Hormuz restrictions?
articles.summary: Iran has exempted ships from India, China, Iraq, and Qatar from restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. A senior Iranian lawmaker stated that Tehran receives medicine and political backing in return, while collecting transit fees from India and China. Analysts suggest the move generates revenue and challenges Washington's naval blockade amid the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Tehran says ships from four countries can cross Hormuz freely, but analysts say the deals carry political risks.

articles.headline: Tech stocks plummet following US midterm election results
articles.title: Global tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to AI slowdown fears
articles.summary: Major technology firms lost over a trillion dollars in market value after US midterm election results sparked fears of an artificial intelligence development slowdown. Shares in companies like Nvidia and Tesla fell sharply as investors reacted to Democratic campaign promises to restrict data center construction. The Nasdaq composite index has now entered official correction territory.
articles.description: Investors have reacted to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the AI industry.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules OBC creamy layer verdict is not retrospective
articles.title: SC clarifies its March 2026 verdict on OBC creamy layer policy will not apply retrospectively
articles.summary: The Supreme Court clarified that its March 2026 judgment regarding OBC non-creamy layer status will not apply retrospectively. The court rejected the government's request for a two-year extension to establish administrative equivalence. The Centre argued that retrospective implementation would cause administrative chaos, affecting past recruitments, seniority, and service allocations across various federal departments.
articles.description: As far as the operation of the 2025 batch was concerned, the Court said the service allocation would be in compliance with the March 2026 judgment

articles.headline: South Africa holds municipal elections amid declining support for governing party
articles.title: South Africa votes as ANC faces further losses and coalition rule looms
articles.summary: South Africa held municipal elections on November 4, 2026, as growing public anger over corruption and failing services threatened the African National Congress. The ruling party fell below 50% support in 2021 and could drop further, potentially leading to unstable coalitions. President Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged governance failures while expressing optimism. Polling stations closed at 9 p.m., with results expected by Sunday.
articles.description: The ANC’s support could fall below 40%, while the Democratic Alliance is projected to gain ground in Johannesburg

articles.headline: Iran says four oil tankers destroyed by naval mines in Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says tankers destroyed after hitting mines in Hormuz
articles.summary: Four oil tankers were destroyed and caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on November 4, 2026, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps. The incident follows U.S. strikes on Iran and warnings from President Masoud Pezeshkian that no one benefits from war. Tehran maintains control over the vital energy conduit and demands concessions from Washington before reopening the passage.
articles.description: It came a day after President Donald Trump said the United States had launched strikes on the Islamic Republic, following reports of a raid on Qeshm, the largest island in the strait

articles.headline: Delhi air quality deteriorates to very poor levels with severe pollution spikes
articles.title: Air quality of Delhi worsens, many parts reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
articles.summary: Delhi air quality remained in the very poor category with a 24-hour average Air Quality Index of 391 reported by the Central Pollution Control Board on Friday. Several areas across the national capital recorded severe pollution levels, while neighboring towns also experienced poor air. Meteorological factors, stubble burning, and festive activities contributed to the worsening conditions.
articles.description: Many parts of the national capital, including IIT Delhi, ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri, witnessed “severe” level air pollution

articles.headline: Iraqi prime minister speaks with Trump to avoid regional conflict
articles.title: Iraq’s al-Zaidi talks to Trump as Baghdad seeks to stay out of war on Iran
articles.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi discussed regional security with United States President Donald Trump, stating that Baghdad will not permit its territory to be used for attacks against neighbours. Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein warned that a renewed war would be disastrous for Iraq, which has already suffered significant oil revenue losses during the conflict.
articles.description: Call comes as Iraq's top diplomat urges armed groups not to join any Iranian retaliation to US attacks.

articles.headline: Paraguayan President Santiago Pena steps down amid banking crisis
articles.title: Santiago Pena, Paraguay President, steps down as banking crisis sows chaos
articles.summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Pena resigned following the Central Bank seizure of Ueno Bank, which froze deposits for approximately three million people. The November 5, 2026 takeover sparked angry protests, clashes with police, and unanimous parliamentary impeachment proceedings over alleged conflicts of interest. Opposition lawmakers criticized the administration for draining the institution. Vice President Pedro Alliana is scheduled to assume leadership of the South American nation.
articles.description: Thousands of Paraguayans gathered outside Congress on Thursday (November 5, 2026) to protest against the President

articles.headline: Four oil tankers destroyed by naval mines in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'
articles.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced on Wednesday that four oil tankers were destroyed after striking naval sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz while attempting to travel through a prohibited southern route. The announcement arrived as United States voters punished Republicans during the midterm elections, prompting Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf to state that the American public had rejected the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: "We endorse this message," Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf says, as Donald Trump acknowledges the conflict's role in the Republican Party's defeat.

articles.headline: Israeli settlers seize eight Palestinian homes in Jericho amid widespread displacement
articles.title: Israeli settlers seize 8 Palestinian homes in Jericho, displacing dozens
articles.summary: United Nations officials condemned an incident where approximately 30 Israeli settlers forcibly took over eight Palestinian homes in the West Bank city of Jericho on Wednesday. According to the UN, the intruders assaulted residents with live ammunition and stones, displacing dozens of families. Meanwhile, regional authorities disputed settler claims that the properties were legally purchased, citing forged documents.
articles.description: UN says settlers reportedly used live ammunition and beat Palestinians, forcing families to flee for their safety.

articles.headline: Paraguay’s president impeached amid bank collapse crisis
articles.title: Paraguay’s president impeached amid bank collapse crisis
articles.description: Lawmakers have voted to impeach Paraguay’s President Santiago Pena amid a banking collapse that has roiled the country.

articles.headline: Zelensky awards Melania Trump for humanitarian support following ceasefire agreement
articles.title: Zelensky gives Melania Trump Ukraine's highest award after Oleshky ceasefire
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky awarded the Order of Princess Olha, 1st Class, to United States First Lady Melania Trump for her humanitarian support. The recognition follows her role in securing a temporary ceasefire in Kherson that enabled evacuations from Oleshky. Russian and Ukrainian delegations are scheduled to meet at the White House on Thursday to discuss ongoing diplomatic efforts and postwar security.
articles.description: Russian and Ukrainian delegations will meet the US first lady at the White House on Thursday.

articles.headline: Iran security chief Mohsen Rezaei meets Vladimir Putin in Moscow
articles.title: Iran’s security chief meets Putin, delivers message from Khamenei
articles.summary: Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow to discuss regional security and deliver a letter from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. According to Iranian state broadcaster Press TV, the talks on Thursday addressed post-war security arrangements, deep energy cooperation including gas pipelines, and ending United States aggression. Rezaei stated that Tehran will not negotiate until seven specific conditions are met by Washington.
articles.description: Putin meets Iran's top security official to discuss regional security and receives a letter from Mojtaba Khamenei.

articles.headline: Trump loses control of Congress
articles.title: Trump loses control of Congress
articles.description: Democrats have made historic gains in the US midterms, dealing a major setback to President Donald Trump.

articles.headline: California Governor Gavin Newsom commutes death row sentences for 548 inmates
articles.title: California governor commutes sentences of more than 500 people on death row
articles.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom announced the largest mass clemency in United States history, commuting the death row sentences of 548 individuals to life imprisonment without parole. Proclaimed on Thursday, the decision effectively empties the state capital punishment population, though twenty-three states have banned the practice entirely. Criminal justice groups praised the move as historic, while the Death Penalty Information Center noted that about two-thirds of the commutations require review by the California Supreme Court.
articles.description: Gavin Newsom cites state values and flaws in the legal system as he grants largest mass clemency in US history.

articles.headline: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman unseats incumbent Karen Bass in Los Angeles
articles.title: Democratic socialist defeats incumbent Karen Bass in Los Angeles mayor's race
articles.summary: Challenger Nithya Raman defeated incumbent mayor Karen Bass in the municipal race in California. Bass conceded the election on Thursday after trailing in the vote count. The outcome brings another high-profile democratic socialist to lead a major American municipality, with the new mayor facing upcoming responsibilities including hosting the Summer Olympic Games in the year 2028.
articles.description: The results mean America's two most populous cities - New York and Los Angeles - will be led by democratic socialists.

articles.headline: Turkish parliament ratifies Mecca defence agreement with collective defence clause
articles.title: Turkiye’s parliament ratifies Mecca defence agreement
articles.summary: Lawmakers in Turkiye approved a mutual defence pact involving Saudi Arabia and Pakistan that mirrors the North Atlantic Treaty Organization Article 5 commitment. The measure secured two hundred seventy-nine votes on Thursday in Ankara. Officials emphasized the framework aims to enhance regional deterrence amid ongoing Houthi strikes rather than engage directly in active combat operations across the Middle East.
articles.description: Parliament's approval lays the groundwork for further Turkish involvement in Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Houthis.

articles.headline: Donald Trump meets Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House
articles.title: Trump says Russia-Ukraine deal is near after meeting Putin’s envoy
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated that a diplomatic accord between Moscow and Kyiv could happen soon following discussions with special envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington. The talks occurred after First Lady Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian officials on Thursday to build upon a previous six-day humanitarian ceasefire negotiated in Oleshky during the month of October.
articles.description: Though the US president said deal was 'very close', he gave no specifics and did not meet visiting Ukrainian delegation.

articles.headline: Nithya Raman defeats Karen Bass in Los Angeles mayoral election
articles.title: Nithya Raman wins LA mayoral race, becoming city’s first South Asian mayor
articles.summary: Progressive city council member Nithya Raman secured a victory over incumbent Karen Bass in the second-largest United States city. The Associated Press called the contest on Thursday after Raman captured fifty-two percent of the ballots. Supported by the Democratic Socialists of America, the Indian-born urban planner will become the first South Asian to lead Los Angeles following a campaign focused on housing and homelessness.
articles.description: DSA-backed Raman will lead the second-largest US city, promising action on homelessness and affordable housing.

articles.headline: Global leaders react as US Democrats win control of Congress
articles.title: ‘Seismic shift’: World reacts to US midterm election results
articles.summary: Foreign governments are evaluating how Democratic control of both chambers of Congress might reshape United States foreign policy following midterm elections. Iranian officials warned against conflict, while European and Asian leaders expressed varied expectations regarding trade, defense, and international alliances. According to local reports, the political shift follows widespread voter concerns over economic pressures and ongoing military engagements.
articles.description: Iran's top negotiator says US voters sent a “NO TO WAR” message, as Trump's Democratic opponents take Congress.

articles.headline: California governor commutes death sentences for all 548 inmates
articles.title: California governor commutes sentences for state's 548 death row inmates
articles.summary: Governor Gavin Newsom has commuted the death sentences of all 548 inmates on California's death row to life imprisonment without parole. Newsom stated that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values and described the capital punishment system as a failure. The move, which requires judicial approval, comes as the Democratic leader concludes his final term.
articles.description: California has historically had the largest population of people on death row in the US.

articles.headline: Democrats win US House majority in midterm elections against Trump
articles.title: Democrats win U.S. House in growing midterms wave against Trump
articles.summary: The Democratic Party secured control of the United States House of Representatives in elections on Tuesday, delivering a sharp rebuke to President Donald Trump. Growing public discontent over inflation, tariffs, and military action against Iran fueled a broad electoral wave, granting the opposition legislative power to block agendas and launch investigations.
articles.description: A Democratic House majority would give the Opposition the power to block Mr. Trump’s legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration during the final two years of his presidency

articles.headline: Democrats win control of House and Senate in midterms
articles.title: Democrats win control of House and Senate: Key US midterms takeaways
articles.summary: During the November 2026 elections, the Democratic Party won control of both the United States House of Representatives and the Senate, dealing a major defeat to President Donald Trump's Republicans. According to the Associated Press, Democrats secured significant victories nationwide, including historic wins such as Michigan electing its first Muslim senator, Abdul El-Sayed.
articles.description: This is the first time in 20 years that a Republican president has lost both houses of US Congress.

articles.headline: Hoax bomb threats force emergency landings, evacuations across Europe
articles.title: Hoax bomb threats force emergency landings, evacuations across Europe
articles.description: Bomb threats are causing travel disruptions at airports across Europe, targeting at least 27 flights.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts ballistic missile fired toward Medina
articles.title: Saudi coalition intercepts missile fired towards Medina
articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting a ballistic missile launched by Houthi rebels toward the Medina region on Thursday. The Houthis denied targeting the city, claiming their operations focus on military and energy infrastructure. Meanwhile, Yemeni government forces reported gains in the Taiz governorate, claiming to have killed approximately 400 Houthi fighters during recent combat operations.
articles.description: Interception comes after Saudi civil defence agency warned of potential danger near the strategic port of Yanbu.

articles.headline: Georgia elects first Black woman governor in US
articles.title: Georgia elects first Black woman governor in US
articles.description: Al Jazeera’s Matthew Torres reports on the historic gubernatorial election win in Georgia.

articles.headline: Mass protests in France driven by nationwide strike action
articles.title: Mass protests in France driven by nationwide strike action
articles.description: More than 250,000 people took to the streets across France on Thursday as five unions called a day of strike action.

articles.headline: Netanyahu faces political instability as US-Israel relations sour
articles.title: The blame game: How the US midterm shock is shaping Israel’s race for PM
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces a difficult path to forming a government following the October 27 election. Opposition leaders blame Netanyahu for deteriorating ties with the United States, which they claim has made Israel politically toxic. While Netanyahu seeks a majority, his traditional allies are wavering, and experts warn that US-Israel relations may remain strained regardless of leadership.
articles.description: The Republican midterm rout is helping shape who leads Israel next, as Netanyahu’s US ties turn toxic.

articles.headline: Melania Trump hosts rare meeting between Russian and Ukrainian officials
articles.title: Melania Trump calls for ‘enduring’ Ukraine truce as rivals meet at White House
articles.summary: United States First Lady Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian officials at the White House on November 5, 2026, to advocate for a permanent ceasefire. The gathering built upon a localised six-day truce in Oleshky that she helped broker last month. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy awarded her the Order of Princess Olga, First Class.
articles.description: The unprecedented meeting hoped to build on a localised six-day truce in the starvation-hit Ukrainian city of Oleshky that U.S. President Donald Trump’s wife had announced last month

articles.headline: US civil rights official Harmeet Dhillon resigns from Justice Department
articles.title: Harmeet Dhillon, top US civil rights official under Trump, resigns
articles.summary: Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon has resigned from the United States Department of Justice, Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed on Thursday. Dhillon, a key ally of President Donald Trump, oversaw the civil rights division since April 2025. Her departure follows Democratic gains in the midterm elections, with lawmakers planning investigations into immigration enforcement and other administration controversies.
articles.description: New Democratic Congress expected to probe Trump Justice Department office's handling of Epstein files and ICE killings.

articles.headline: Democrats sweep US midterms to secure full control of Congress
articles.title: Democrats deliver a historic routing to Republicans in US midterms
articles.summary: United States voters delivered a historic rebuke to President Donald Trump during Tuesday midterm elections, handing Democrats control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate after flipping multiple seats across the country. Economic grievances regarding high petrol and grocery prices, which surged following the launch of a war on Iran in February, heavily drove the voter backlash against the Republican Party.
articles.description: For the first time in nearly 30 years, a Democrat will now represent South Carolina in the US Senate.

articles.headline: Police search for suspect after eight killed in Turkiye
articles.title: Eight killed in series of shootings in western Turkey
articles.summary: A large-scale manhunt is underway in the Afyonkarahisar province of western Turkiye following a series of shootings that left eight people dead and one injured on Thursday. Victims were discovered in three separate vehicles across different locations. Police have closed roads in the area as they search for the suspect, who reportedly abandoned a vehicle and fled.
articles.description: Victims are found in several locations in three separate vehicles, according to local reports.

articles.headline: Melania Trump hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials to discuss peace
articles.title: Melania Trump calls for peace at meeting with Russia, Ukraine officials
articles.summary: United States First Lady Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian representatives at the White House on Thursday to encourage an enduring peace. The meeting followed a recent six-day ceasefire in Oleshky, which allowed for aid deliveries and evacuations. New talks are scheduled for November 10 and 11 in Abu Dhabi to address the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: US first lady hosts Russian, Ukrainian officials at the White House, urges two sides to build on recent local truce.

articles.headline: Democrats capture Congress in midterm upset and outline priorities
articles.title: Democrats win Congress: How they did it, and what it means
articles.summary: The Democratic Party secured comfortable majorities in both the Senate and the House of Representatives during the United States midterm elections, flipping multiple critical seats. While the newly achieved legislative control empowers Democrats to block presidential appointments and launch congressional investigations, President Donald Trump has already signalled his intention to utilize his veto power extensively against their policy agenda.
articles.description: With control of Congress, Democrats can challenge Trump’s agenda through subpoenas, confirmation votes.

articles.headline: Eight people killed in rural Turkiye shooting attacks
articles.title: Eight dead in mass shooting in rural west Turkiye: officials
articles.summary: Eight people were killed and one person was critically injured in armed attacks across three villages near Afyonkarahisar, Turkiye, on Thursday. Police have launched a major manhunt for the suspect, who was seen in CCTV footage carrying a rifle. Authorities are investigating potential links to an earlier shooting incident that occurred in the town center of Afyonkarahisar.
articles.description: The shooting struck in a rural area near Afyonkarahisar, a town halfway between the capital Ankara and the coastal city of Izmir

articles.headline: India mandates visas for undocumented minority migrants
articles.title: Visa must for undocumented six non-Muslim communities who entered India before December 31, 2024: Home Ministry
articles.summary: The Indian Ministry of Home Affairs has amended the Immigration and Foreigners Order to require undocumented non-Muslim migrants from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan who entered India before December 31, 2024, to obtain visas for continued stay. The notification also updates travel document requirements for Indian, Nepali, and Bhutanese citizens crossing borders and clarifies various refugee exemption categories.
articles.description: The amendment applies to members of six non-Muslim communities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who, fearing “religious persecution”, entered India without valid travel documents, or whose documents have since expired

articles.headline: India defeats Japan to retain Asian Champions Trophy crown
articles.title: Asian Champions Trophy: India retains crown with a late surge
articles.summary: India defeated Japan 4-1 at the Olympian Balbir Singh international stadium on Thursday to defend its Asian Champions Trophy title. Kazumasa Matsumoto opened the scoring for Japan in the third minute before Shilanand Lakra equalised in the 42nd minute. Further goals from Dilpreet Singh, Jugraj Singh, and Vivek Sagar Prasad secured the victory for India. Earlier, Malaysia claimed the bronze medal by beating Korea 5-2.
articles.description: The host pumps in four goal in the last 18 minutes to get the better of Japan; Malaysia finishes third

articles.headline: Democratic Party gains US House majority in 2026 midterm elections
articles.title: Democratic Party gains US House majority in 2026 midterm elections
articles.summary: Following the midterm elections, the Democratic Party has secured control of the United States House of Representatives after gaining five seats. The victory positions New York Representative Hakeem Jeffries to potentially become the speaker of the House, succeeding Republican Mike Johnson. The newly elected 120th Congress is scheduled to be sworn in on January 3, 2027, ending a period of Republican unified power in Washington, DC.
articles.description: All 435 seats in the lower chamber of Congress were on the ballot in Tuesday's midterm race.

articles.headline: Government considers panel to review higher education equity regulations
articles.title: Centre tells Supreme Court it may set up a panel to review UGC equity on campus regulations
articles.summary: The Indian government informed the Supreme Court on November 5, 2026, that it is considering forming a special committee to re-examine the 2026 University Grants Commission regulations. These rules, intended to combat campus discrimination, were previously stayed by the court for being overly broad. The regulations were prompted by petitions regarding caste-based bias in universities.
articles.description: The Centre said it was examining criticism about the Regulations, which had sparked protests by upper-caste student groups; the Court had stayed the regulations in January, stating that they were “too vague”

articles.headline: Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam appeal for bail in Delhi
articles.title: Umar, Sharjeel move Supreme Court seeking bail in 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case
articles.summary: Activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have petitioned the Supreme Court of India to challenge a Delhi High Court order denying them bail in the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case. The pair argue that their six-year incarceration without trial violates constitutional liberty, noting that the one-year restriction on filing fresh bail applications is nearing its expiration.
articles.description: In their petitions, the two have contended that their continued incarceration for over six years, with the trial yet to commence, violates the Constitutional guarantee of personal liberty under Article 21

articles.headline: Bharti Airtel reports 24 percent profit increase for September quarter
articles.title: Bharti Airtel net profit rises 24% to ₹10,710 crore in September quarter
articles.summary: Telecom operator Bharti Airtel announced a 24 percent rise in consolidated profit to 10,710 crore rupees for the quarter ending September 2026. Revenue grew by 16.7 percent, supported by higher average revenue per user following tariff adjustments. The company also reported an 11 percent increase in its global customer base, reaching 69.25 crore total subscribers.
articles.description: Bharti Airtel's India revenue grew by 9.4% to ₹42,308 crore

articles.headline: Arab party backs Eisenkot in bid to form Israel’s next government
articles.title: Arab party backs Eisenkot in bid to form Israel’s next government
articles.description: Arab-majority party Ra’am and the Democrats have backed Gadi Eisenkot in a bid to form Israel’s next government.

articles.headline: Government clarifies Agnipath scheme has not been rolled back
articles.title: Agniveer scheme not rolled back, all eligible recruits to be absorbed after six years: MoD
articles.summary: On November 5, 2026, the Indian government clarified that the Agnipath scheme remains active following a recent two-year engagement extension. Ministry of Defence sources stated that all willing Agniveers meeting eligibility criteria will eventually be absorbed into the regular armed forces without a numerical cap. Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh described the revision as a beneficial arrangement that protects seniority and rewards exceptional performance.
articles.description: 75% Agniveers to get second two-year engagement; seniority to be protected on absorption into regular cadre

articles.headline: Democrats secure historic midterm victory giving Donald Trump lame-duck status
articles.title: A new political balance in Washington
articles.summary: Democrats achieved a decisive victory in the United States midterm elections on November 4, projected to win the national popular vote for the House of Representatives by nearly 13 percent. The electoral shift follows widespread economic dissatisfaction linked to President Donald Trump's reciprocal tariffs and military actions in Iran, leaving him facing a potential legislative blockade.
articles.description: The Democrats’ midterm victory gives them an opportunity to check Trump’s unilateral policies through congressional oversight and legislative powers; a weakened Trump Administration could also give India greater leverage in bilateral trade negotiations

articles.headline: NPCI defends new merchant discount rate charge in Supreme Court
articles.title: NPCI says MDR charge has been imposed to save the UPI ecosystem from turning ouroboric
articles.summary: The National Payments Corporation of India defended its newly introduced merchant discount rate in the Supreme Court on November 5, 2026. Represented by Additional Solicitor General N. Venkataraman, the corporation stated that zero-MDR was unsustainable for the expanding Unified Payments Interface ecosystem. The amended framework imposes a 0.4 percent charge on person-to-merchant transactions exceeding two thousand rupees while keeping ninety-six percent of merchant payments and all peer-to-peer transactions entirely free.
articles.description: Zero MDR is no longer sustainable; the magnitude of growth places correspondingly greater demands on the security, resilience, and infrastructural capacity of the system, NCPI tells SC

articles.headline: United States markets slide as technology sector leads heavy losses
articles.title: AI stocks plunge after US election, driving down markets
articles.summary: United States markets declined sharply on Thursday following sweeping Democratic midterm election victories.
