articles.summary: The Women's Tennis Association announced round-robin groups for the season-ending championships scheduled to run through November 15 at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. Top-seeded Elena Rybakina, fourth-seeded Coco Gauff, fifth-seeded Jessica Pegula and eighth-seeded Linda Noskova were drawn into Group-1, while Aryna Sabalenka heads Group 2 ahead of tournament matches beginning on Sunday.
articles.description: Each player and team will face the other three in their group over the first six days, with the top two advancing to semifinals

articles.headline: Africa’s richest man launches mega oil tank farm in Namibia
articles.title: Africa’s richest man launches mega oil tank farm in Namibia
articles.description: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote launched a fuel storage facility in Namibia to future-proof Southern Africa's supply.

articles.headline: Guinea-Bissau cancels US-funded hepatitis B vaccine trial on newborns
articles.title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau
articles.summary: Guinea-Bissau authorities cancelled a proposed hepatitis B vaccine trial involving 14,000 newborns after critics labeled the study unethical and neocolonial. The trial, funded by the US, planned to withhold WHO-recommended vaccines from half the participants. Police have seized vaccine batches at the Bandim Health Project, while the government maintains the study lacked proper local authorization.
articles.description: The trial was condemned as "unethical" and "neocolonial" because half of the babies would not be given the vaccine.

articles.headline: Who gets to vote in the US?
articles.title: Who gets to vote in the US?
articles.description: Tati Abu King lost his voting rights after felony convictions.

articles.headline: Giant banner of Trump, Vance and Netanyahu burnt at Tehran rally
articles.title: Giant banner of Trump, Vance and Netanyahu burnt at Tehran rally
articles.description: A giant banner depicting US President Donald Trump and Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was burnt in Tehran

articles.headline: Intense typhoons batter East Asia amid record-breaking El Nino conditions
articles.title: Typhoons batter East Asia as El Niño makes Pacific 'burn with fever'
articles.summary: Severe storms exacerbated by the El Nino weather pattern have caused widespread destruction across the Philippines, Taiwan, China, and Japan, killing dozens and disrupting transport. Experts warn that record-high Pacific Ocean temperatures are supercharging typhoon energy, leading to heavier rainfall and stronger winds. Governments across the region are implementing emergency preparedness measures while long-term climate adaptation remains a critical challenge.
articles.description: Even for countries where typhoons are a way of life, the last few months have brought unusually wild weather.

articles.headline: Democratic Socialists of America achieve record federal election wins
articles.title: Democratic Socialists of America see record wins in US midterm elections
articles.summary: Candidates backed by or affiliated with the Democratic Socialists of America secured a record number of federal office victories in the recent United States midterm elections, marking the movement's most successful national performance. Figures including Claire Valdez, Darializa Avila Chevalier, Brad Lander, and returning incumbents won congressional seats across states such as New York, Michigan, and Colorado.
articles.description: The left-wing movement has won support for its views on issues like the war in Gaza and universal healthcare.

articles.headline: Satellite data reveals dramatic reduction in Bhutan glacial lake after flood
articles.title: Satellite assessment shows 73% reduction in Bhutan’s lake after GLOF
articles.summary: An analysis by Noida-based geospatial firm Suhora Technologies shows that Bhutan's Sintaphu Tsho shrank by seventy-three percent following an October twenty-ninth glacial lake outburst flood in the Gasa district. The disaster destroyed facilities at Gasa Tshachu and triggered warnings in India. Researchers emphasize that continuous satellite monitoring is vital for assessing Himalayan environmental risks and improving disaster preparedness.
articles.description: The Noida-based geospatial intelligence company’s study indicates a supraglacial lake adjoining the GLOF-hit Sintaphu Tsho continues to remain substantially larger than its 2016 extent

articles.headline: Qualcomm targets data center expansion as smartphone sales decline globally
articles.title: Qualcomm is betting big on data centers as smartphone sales sink
articles.summary: Amid a roughly 20 percent decline in smartphone sales compared to 2025, technology firm Qualcomm is expanding into artificial intelligence data centers through partnerships with companies like Amazon and Meta. During its fourth quarter 2026 earnings call, the company projected $650 million in data center revenue for the first quarter of 2027, anticipating that this segment will eventually reach $5 billion by the end of 2027 and account for 30 percent of its business by 2029.
articles.description: With smartphone sales tanking by around 20 percent compared to 2025, Qualcomm is looking to data centers to help boost its bottom line. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company laid out its plans to make a splash in the AI data center business, through partnerships with companies like Amazon and Meta announced earlier […]

articles.headline: 'Hopefully things get done': Americans react to historic political shift
articles.title: 'Hopefully things get done': Americans react to historic political shift
articles.description: The BBC spoke to voters from different states for their reaction to Democrats taking control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives.

articles.headline: Sudanese factories struggle to resume operations following severe wartime damage in Khartoum
articles.title: Sudan factories struggle to restart after devastating wartime losses
articles.summary: More than three years after fighting began in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces, factory owner Mansour Gaily reported $1 million in losses and operates at 40 percent capacity in Khartoum. According to Sudan’s Ministry of Industry, approximately 1,800 industrial facilities were damaged, with 650 completely destroyed, leaving less than 10 percent operational while manufacturers face severe shortages of raw materials, electricity, and financing.
articles.description: War has left Sudanese workers jobless and consumers facing higher prices as factories struggle to reopen.

articles.headline: Palestinians, Israelis react after Democrats sweep US midterms
articles.title: Palestinians, Israelis react after Democrats sweep US midterms
articles.description: Palestinians and Israelis are divided in their opinion following the win by Democrats in the US midterm elections.

articles.headline: Punjab and Haryana High Court directs schools to address LGBTQIA+ bullying and harassment
articles.title: Schools must address bullying based on gender identity, sexual orientation: High Court
articles.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court directed the Haryana Department of School Education and the Central Board of Education to ensure regional schools comply with Supreme Court guidelines regarding bullying based on gender identity and sexual orientation. The ruling followed a petition by the mother of a 16-year-old Faridabad student who died on February 24, 2022, after reportedly facing physical assault and harassment by peers who misunderstood his artistic inclination.
articles.description: The court gave directions after hearing a petition by the mother of a 16-year-old boy, a student of a prominent school in Faridabad, who died on February 24, 2022, accusing the school authorities and the headmistress of it

articles.headline: Kiren Rijiju sets conditions for Congress to increase parliamentary seats
articles.title: Spend more time in India: Rijiju takes jibe at Rahul, list conditions for Congress to ‘win more MPs’
articles.summary: Union minister Kiren Rijiju outlined seven conditions for the opposition party on November 4, 2026, advising senior leader Rahul Gandhi to spend more time in the country and avoid meetings with anti-India individuals. The remarks followed a public challenge by Mr. Gandhi for Prime Minister Narendra Modi to participate in an open debate, which also drew criticism from other Bharatiya Janata Party leaders.
articles.description: Kiren Rijiju has been taking on Rahul Gandhi and other Congress leaders for demanding an open debate with the Prime Minister

articles.headline: Democrat leaders hail midterm election success
articles.title: Democrat leaders hail midterm election success
articles.description: The top Democrats in the two chambers of US Congress have been hailing their party’s resounding victory in the midterms.

articles.headline: Bihar completes construction of over 43 lakh pucca houses for poor families
articles.title: More than 43 lakh pucca houses completed in Bihar for poor families
articles.summary: A total of 4314959 poor families in Bihar completed the construction of pucca houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana Gramin scheme. According to the Rural Development Department figures, approvals were granted for 4909740 beneficiaries against a target of 4916649 houses. The state government spent 5674340 crore rupees on implementing the flagship initiative to provide essential shelter with basic amenities.
articles.description: ₹56,743.40 crore spent under PMAY-G so far in the State; of the 43 lakh houses, 36.63 lakh pucca houses built in just yearrs between FY 2016-17 & 2021-22

articles.headline: Explosion damages Anupgarh Suratgarh railway track in northern Rajasthan
articles.title: Explosion damages railway track in northern Rajasthan district
articles.summary: A powerful explosion damaged the Anupgarh Suratgarh railway track in Sriganganagar district on November 3, 2026, creating a two-foot-deep crater and prompting a sabotage investigation. North-Western Railway cancelled four train services as security agencies and forensic experts examined the site. Sriganganagar Superintendent of Police Harishankar Yadav confirmed that National Investigation Agency and Anti-Terrorism Squad teams joined the ongoing probe.
articles.description: The blast, which occurred near 50 GB village, shattered two concrete railway sleepers beneath the tracks, dislodged the track clips and created a two-foot-deep crater at the site

articles.headline: Government proposes immediate suspension of manufacturing licences for substandard drugs
articles.title: Government proposes immediate suspension of manufacturing licences of substandard drugs
articles.summary: The Union Health Ministry proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, allowing authorities to immediately suspend manufacturing licences for medicines declared substandard on critical quality parameters. Announced on November 4, 2026, the regulatory changes aim to prevent the distribution of risky medications, mandate root-cause analysis before revocation, and improve communication among stakeholders.
articles.description: Proposed amendment provides for mandatory corrective measures before revocation of the suspension; suspension shall continue until the manufacturer undertakes corrective action

articles.headline: NDA alliance leaders celebrate municipal corporation election victory in Vijayawada
articles.title: Celebrations among NDA alliance leaders after landslide victory
articles.summary: Alliance leaders and workers celebrated an emphatic electoral win in the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation elections on Wednesday. Participants including MP Kesineni Sivanath and MLAs felicitated the newly elected Mayor Vangaveeti Radha Krishna, expressing commitment to urban development despite low voter turnout and seat-sharing delays during the contest.

articles.headline: Democratic progressive candidate Randy Villegas wins California congressional district race
articles.title: Democratic progressive wing notches win in California Central Valley
articles.summary: Democratic educator Randy Villegas defeated Republican incumbent David Valadao in California’s 22nd congressional district on Tuesday evening. Backed by progressive figures like Senator Bernie Sanders, the campaign focused on the rising cost of living, healthcare cuts, and public backlash against immigration raids conducted by the federal government.
articles.description: Campaign focused on cost of living issues and backlash over ICE raids pays dividends for progressive Randy Villegas.

articles.headline: Madras High Court petition seeks guidelines for police handling social media speech
articles.title: Direct T.N. DGP to frame guidelines regarding registration of criminal cases for social media posts, political criticism and online speech, insists a PIL plea before Madras High Court
articles.summary: A public interest litigation petition filed before the Madras High Court asks for uniform guidelines for police officers handling complaints regarding social media posts and political criticism. Petitioner H. Syed Alim cited instances of mechanical case registration against commentators and noted that the Supreme Court previously upheld similar guidelines set by the Telangana High Court.
articles.description: Litigant says the Telangana High Court had framed a set of guidelines last year for the police in the neighbouring State and that Tamil Nadu could take a cue from that judgment

articles.headline: Two youths booked under POCSO Act after party assault in Balanagar
articles.title: Two 17-year-old students sexually assaulted at party, two booked under PoCSO
articles.summary: Madinaguda police registered a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act against two youths following the alleged sexual assault of two seventeen-year-old students on October 1, 2026. According to police inspector H. Prabhakar, the suspects allegedly gave the victims alcohol at a party in Balanagar. One victim fell ill, leading to hospitalization and the subsequent filing of a formal complaint.

articles.headline: Karnataka to integrate skilling efforts into single unified system
articles.title: Karnataka will integrate all its skilling efforts into a single unified system: CM
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announced a plan on November 5, 2026, to merge fragmented skilling initiatives into a unified system with an estimated investment of five thousand crore rupees to train thirty lakh people over seven years. Speaking at the Bengaluru Skill Summit, Shivakumar also launched Udyoga Sethu, an artificial intelligence-powered digital employment platform designed to connect local job seekers with verified private-sector employers.
articles.description: To reshape State’s workforce pipeline, government will allocate ₹5,000 crore to streamline its fragmented skilling initiatives spread across various departments and entities and also train 30 lakh beneficiaries over the next seven years

articles.headline: World Health Organization approves clinical trials for two new Ebola vaccines
articles.title: WHO approves trials for two new Ebola vaccines
articles.summary: The World Health Organization approved clinical trials for two new vaccines targeting the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus amid an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Led by the National Institute for Biomedical Research, the trials follow more than 5,300 deaths, with results expected in early 2027 according to the global health agency.
articles.description: Two new vaccines were designed for the Bundibugyo virus that has killed more than 5,300 in the DR Congo.

articles.headline: Subroto Bagchi calls for immediate overhaul of vocational ecosystem
articles.title: Subroto Bagchi calls for immediate overhaul of India’s vocational ecosystem
articles.summary: Subroto Bagchi, chairman of Karnataka's Vision Group for Skill Development, urged an immediate overhaul of India's vocational ecosystem on November 4, 2026, addressing wage disparity and class prejudice. Speaking at the Bengaluru Skill Summit, the Mindtree co-founder contrasted low graduate pay with mandatory minimum wages, criticized societal stigma toward vocational trades, and highlighted the severe underrepresentation of women in technical institutions.
articles.description: Subroto Bagchi condemns the pervasive middle-class habit of labelling household helps as ‘servant maids’ and laments the persistent stigmas that treat vocational institutions as destinations only for youth who have ‘gone astray’

articles.headline: Unresolved US midterm races feature tight margins across multiple states and localities
articles.title: US midterms 2026: What key races remain undecided?
articles.summary: Several pivotal contests from the November 4 election remain undecided amidst narrow vote margins. In Alaska, Senator Dan Sullivan faces Mary Peltola, while Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins contends with Bernadette Wilson. Kansas governor race features Cindy Holscher leading Ty Masterson. Mississippi sees Scott Colom ahead of Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, and Los Angeles has Karen Bass trailing Nithya Raman as tabulation continues across these key jurisdictions.
articles.description: Ballots continue to be counted in states like Alaska, Mississippi, Kansas and California for toss-up races.

articles.headline: Kerala political parties clash over rapid issuance of bar licences by officials
articles.title: CPI(M) and Congress skirmish over 'hasty issuance' of liquor licences in Keralam
articles.summary: Political tensions intensified on November 5, 2026, as the ruling United Democratic Front and the opposition Communist Party of India (Marxist) traded accusations regarding the swift distribution of bar permits. Administration officials allegedly bypassed ministerial authority while processing licences, prompting concerns from religious groups and accusations of political evasion from senior state ministers.
articles.description: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and Excise Minister M. Liju blame the LDF government for the 'liberal granting' of bar licences by ceding the authority to lower-level excise officials, possibly to evade political responsibility; CPI(M) State Secretariat member and former Excise Minister M.B. Rajesh accuses Satheesan and Liju of 'lying' to save face, and the LDF had granted liquor licences only with the Minister’s sanction

articles.headline: Kimi Antonelli becomes the youngest champion in Formula One history
articles.title: Kimi Antonelli - A new face for a new era
articles.summary: Driver Kimi Antonelli secured the Formula One world championship, becoming the youngest titleholder in the sport's history and the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Millions of viewers across Italy watched the historic victory on television, marking a significant milestone for the motorsport-passionate nation during a modern era of racing.
articles.description: Mercedes team boss punted on the Italian and backed him through a bruising rookie year, a barrage of doubts and a few departing sponsors. But he never once wavered in his belief. The youngest champion in F1 history has repaid that faith, and silenced the critics along the way

articles.headline: Supreme Court judicial safeguards in death penalty cases
articles.title: How the Supreme Court shaped due process in death penalty cases
articles.summary: On November 4, 2026, reports reviewed how the Supreme Court's 1980 guidelines from the Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab ruling have functioned over four decades. The Constitution Bench mandated that life imprisonment remains the norm, allowing death sentences only for special reasons where life terms are foreclosed, aligning with provisions in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
articles.description: In Bachan Singh, the apex court upheld the death penalty but laid down guidelines for judicial discretion; in Manoj v. State of Madhya Pradesh, it prescribed ‘practical guidelines’, including the submission of mental health evaluations and custody conduct reports of the accused

articles.headline: India's 2027 census criteria for urban settlements
articles.title: Need for a unified urbanisation plan
articles.summary: Published on November 4, 2026, details emerged regarding India's upcoming 2027 Census classifications. Settlements will be designated as urban if notified as statutory towns or if they meet specific criteria, including a minimum population of 5,000, a density of 400 persons per square kilometre, and at least 75 percent male workers in non-agricultural employment.
articles.description: The Union Budget, Economic Survey and Finance Commission recognise that India is urbanising across a rural-urban continuum. Yet Census 2027 will use the 2011 definitions, deepening the undercount of urban India; a National Urbanisation Policy can recognise this gap and build the institutional and fiscal mechanisms to bridge it

articles.headline: DMK president Stalin criticises TVK administration in Coimbatore
articles.title: Stalin dubs TVK government a ‘circus’ controlled by corporate interests
articles.summary: On November 4, 2026, Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam president M.K. Stalin addressed a gathering in Coimbatore, alleging that corporate power centres control the TVK-led government and Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. He criticised the administration over power cuts, rising crime rates, and the arrest of a party functionary in a drug trafficking case, while defending recent anti-corruption searches.
articles.description: Chief Minister is unable to take independent decisions, and corporate interests are influencing the functioning of the government, says DMK president

articles.headline: Bombay High Court denies bail in fatal lynching case
articles.title: Bombay HC denies bail in lynching case, says only law can punish offenders
articles.summary: On October 28, 2026, the Bombay High Court rejected bail for Sharad Digambar Gorane in connection with a fatal lynching. Justice Milind Jadhav emphasised that personal rivalries and a victim's criminal background do not justify mob violence or vigilantism, noting the severity of the 38 injuries inflicted during the attack inside the victim's residence.
articles.description: Rejecting the argument that the victim was a history-sheeter, the court says his antecedents cannot justify vengeance or mob justice

articles.headline: India defeats Korea to reach Asian Champions Trophy final
articles.title: ACT Hockey: Dominant India storms into the final
articles.summary: India secured a place in the final of the Asian Champions Trophy after defeating Korea 8-1 at the Olympian Balbir Singh International Stadium on November 4, 2026. The dominant victory sets up a title clash against Japan, which advanced by overcoming Malaysia in a penalty shoot-out following a scoreless regulation match.

articles.headline: Kerala High Court rules political activities are prohibited in academic institutions
articles.title: Political activities have no place in educational institutions: Keralam HC
articles.summary: The Kerala High Court overturned a previous ruling that allowed sixteen Students’ Federation of India activists to participate in semester examinations at the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady. Justices Anil K. Narendran and S. Muralee Krishna emphasised that political actions are incompatible with educational environments and upheld the consequences of student suspensions.
articles.description: A Division Bench quashed a Single Bench order that had allowed 16 SFI activists to appear for semester examinations at Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady

articles.headline: Danish students strike and protest against proposed government stipend cuts
articles.title: Danish students join European protest wave against education funding cuts
articles.summary: Thousands of students across Denmark participated in demonstrations and strikes on November 2, 2026, opposing government proposals to reduce student allowances in order to reallocate funds for defense spending. The demonstrations mirror broader youth unrest across Europe regarding economic pressures, with officials estimating that thousands of individuals will experience stipend reductions or losses.
articles.description: Danish government proposes scrapping allowance scheme for students from wealthier families.

articles.headline: North Korea fires multiple missiles following dispute over cryptocurrency heist
articles.title: North Korea fires missiles after rejecting U.S. claims over Binance hack
articles.summary: South Korea reported that North Korea launched several missiles toward its eastern waters on November 4, 2026, shortly after Pyongyang rejected United States accusations implicating its hackers in a major cryptocurrency exchange theft at Binance. The missile activity coincides with heightened regional tensions, border security disputes, and ongoing efforts by North Korea to advance its military capabilities.
articles.description: Pyongyang said it had no need to resume diplomacy with Washington after the FBI blamed North Korean hackers for a cryptocurrency theft

articles.headline: Congress criticises weakening of grievance redressal rules under rural employment programme
articles.title: Congress slams dilution of grievance redressal rules under rural jobs scheme
articles.summary: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh criticised the government for weakening the grievance redressal mechanism under the Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission. Speaking on November 4, 2026, Ramesh stated that final rules dropped key clauses like mandatory first information report filings and local body reviews, reducing transparency and transparency for rural workers.
articles.description: Dropping of key accountability provisions is just another step towards reducing a “rights-based” law into an administrative scheme, says Congress leader Jairam Ramesh

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi inaugurates Pune Metro Line 3 and outlines expansion
articles.title: PM Modi inaugurates Pune Metro Line 3, says expansion will boost connectivity, economic growth
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated on Tuesday that India's operational metro network expanded from 248 kilometers in 2014 to 1,200 kilometers across 26 cities. Speaking via video conference for the Pink Line launch in Pune, he laid foundation stones for Phase-II projects worth approximately 21,800 crores. Modi emphasized that enhanced urban transit infrastructure directly improves citizen convenience and accelerates national economic growth.
articles.description: The Prime Minister inaugurated Pune Metro Line 3 (Pink Line) and laid the foundation stone of four new metro corridors under Phase-II, via video conferencing

articles.headline: Telugu Desam Party wins all four municipal corporations across Rayalaseema
articles.title: TDP sweeps four Municipal Corporations across Rayalaseema
articles.summary: The Telugu Desam Party secured victories in four municipal corporation mayoral races across Tirupati, Kadapa, Nellore, and Ongole. In Tirupati, candidate Manne Srinivasa Prasad defeated his YSR Congress Party opponent by over sixty-one thousand votes, capturing thirty-eight of sixty-six wards. Similar decisive majorities across Kadapa, Nellore, and Ongole enabled the Telugu Desam Party to dominate the municipal councils while opposition parties secured far fewer seats.
articles.description: Ruling party emerges victorious in Tirupati, Kadapa, Nellore and Ongole; YSRCP, which swept across wards in 2021 Municipal polls in Kadapa and Nellore, won just one ward in each corporation

articles.headline: Bangladesh wage board agrees to revise garment worker pay structure from December
articles.title: Bangladesh agrees new garment pay scale from December amid protests
articles.summary: Bangladesh's newly formed wage board agreed on November 4, 2026, to implement a revised pay scale for garment workers starting in December following five days of protests and labour unrest. Workers have demanded an increase in the monthly minimum wage from 12,500 taka to 30,000 taka. Clashes occurred in Savar and Gazipur as protests disrupted spring and summer export order production.
articles.description: Workers are demanding the monthly minimum wage be raised to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, saying rising food, housing and transport costs have eroded their purchasing power

articles.headline: India approves Rs 2,814 crore scheme to boost lithium and nickel processing
articles.title: Centre earmarks ₹2,814 crore to boost lithium, nickel processing
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a capital expenditure support scheme worth 2,814 crore rupees to establish domestic processing facilities for lithium and nickel. Union Minister for Coal and Industries G. Kishan Reddy stated the initiative will reduce import dependence and strengthen industries like electronics. The Federation of Indian Mineral Industries welcomed the move while highlighting the need for secure raw material supplies.
articles.description: In a social media post, Union Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy stated the scheme would help strengthen domestic capabilities, boost manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports.

articles.headline: Mercedes-Benz announces new investments and launches electric GLC in India
articles.title: Mercedes-Benz Group AG to scale up technology, components sourcing from India; launches electric GLC starting ₹78.5 lakh
articles.summary: Mercedes-Benz Group AG Chairman Ola Kallenius announced a fresh investment of 200 crore rupees, bringing total investments to 3,200 crore rupees, and launched the electric GLC sport utility vehicle starting at 78.5 lakh rupees on Wednesday. Kallenius stated the company intends to source more technology and components from India for global operations and expand its Bengaluru research and development center, though full vehicle exports await further volume growth.

articles.headline: Palestinian citizens of Israel face security crackdown after record election success
articles.title: Palestinian citizens of Israel face intimidation after election success
articles.summary: Israeli certification of election results revealed a record 19 seats for Palestinian-led parties, sparking aggressive police raids, arbitrary arrests, and interrogations. While Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and allies alleged electoral fraud, analysts and politicians described the security crackdown as a systematic backlash against the political gains made by Arab citizens.
articles.description: After winning a record number of parliament seats, Palestinian-led parties face campaign against them.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh chief minister surveys rain-affected districts in aerial tour
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh CM Chandrababu Naidu conducts aerial survey of rain-hit areas
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu conducted an aerial survey over rain-impacted areas in Guntur, Bapatla, and Prakasam districts to assess flood conditions. During a review meeting at the Real Time Governance Society, he instructed District Collectors to clear water-logging in locations such as Karamchedu and Chirala to restore normal traffic movement. Officials also reported heavy rains and overflowing tanks in tribal areas of Eluru district.
articles.description: The Chief Minister orders the Collectors concerned to initiate steps to drain stagnant rainwater and prevent disruption to road traffic

articles.headline: Telugu Desam Party-led alliance wins 12 of 13 mayoral posts in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh local body polls: TDP-led NDA wrests 12 of 13 Mayor posts; Anantapur only solace for YSRCP
articles.summary: The Telugu Desam Party-led National Democratic Alliance secured twelve out of thirteen mayoral positions and nearly two-thirds of wards in urban local body elections across Andhra Pradesh on November 4, 2026. The results dealt a blow to the YSR Congress Party, which won only the Anantapur mayoral post. Polling covered thirteen municipal corporations and eighty-seven municipalities amid disruptions from two cyclones.
articles.description: TDP wins 2,571 of 3,897 wards for which poll results have been declared, while YSRCP secures 550 wards, JSP emerges victorious in 484 wards, and BJP grabs 153 wards; counting for Chirala municipality postponed to November 6

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate raids Ragam Theatre in Thrissur over alleged financial fraud
articles.title: ED raids Ragam Theatre in Thrissur in connection with BLM financial fraud case
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate raided Ragam Theatre in Thrissur on November 4, 2026, as part of broader operations concerning the Bharat Lajna Multi-State Housing Co-operative Society financial fraud case. Authorities are investigating allegations that society founder R. Premkumar and associates diverted nearly three hundred crore rupees from depositors, using funds to purchase properties and private company assets.

articles.headline: Nandan Nilekani meets Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu to discuss examination reforms
articles.title: Nandan Nilekani calls on Naidu, discusses reforms in examination system
articles.summary: High-Powered Task Force on Examination Reforms Chairman Nandan Nilekani met Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu at the Secretariat on November 4, 2026. The discussions focused on overhauling India's examination system to improve transparency and security. Mr. Nilekani sought details on Andhra Pradesh testing procedures, while IT and HRD Minister Nara Lokesh explained new methods used in recruitment examinations.
articles.description: While the Chief Minister bats for reforms that ultimately improve employment opportunities, HRD Minister Lokesh briefs the Chairman of the High-Powered Task Force on Examination Reforms about the use of technology in the State to improve efficiency and transparency

articles.headline: Apollo Hospitals reports a 32 percent increase in net profit
articles.title: Apollo Hospitals’ Q2 revenue rises 23%; profit up 32% on broad-based growth
articles.summary: Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd reported a consolidated net profit of 630 crore rupees for the second quarter of the 2027 fiscal year, driven by higher patient volumes and growth across its hospital, pharmacy, and digital businesses. Managing Director Suneeta Reddy stated that international patient revenue rose 37 percent, contributing to overall financial gains across multiple key medical specialties.
articles.description: Hospital business revenue grows 23% as occupancy improves to 73%; international patient revenue rises 37%; Apollo plans to add nearly 5,800 beds over five years

articles.headline: Indian stock markets extend winning streak despite elevated volatility index
articles.title: VIX stays elevated despite five-day market rally as global risks keep investors on edge
articles.summary: Indian stock markets extended a winning streak for five consecutive sessions on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, as the Sensex gained 383 points to close at 77,301. Despite the recovery, the volatility index remained near 15 points due to global uncertainties, crude oil price fluctuations, and outcomes from United States midterm elections.
articles.description: Post the U.S. midterm elections, investor focus will shift to the U.S. administration’s next course of action on West Asia.

articles.headline: Young politicians with African roots win historic races in US midterms
articles.title: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed, Melat Kiros, Adrian Boafo, Junior Ezeonu, and Carol Kazeem are among several politicians with African roots who won seats in the United States midterm elections. The victors campaigned on progressive platforms focusing on the cost of living, universal childcare, and Medicare for All, while breaking historic representation barriers across federal, state, and local governments.
articles.description: For some young Africans, these victories offer a glimpse of what a new generation of voters could do at home.

articles.headline: Garment worker protests narrow Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's window for India visit
articles.title: ‘Garment workers unrest narrows Tarique Rahman’s window for India visit’
articles.summary: Ongoing readymade garment worker protests in Bangladesh are narrowing the window for Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to visit India, according to an anonymous high-level official source speaking to The Hindu on November 4, 2026. The source stated that domestic economic pressure and administrative challenges in Dhaka are exposing government weaknesses and complicating foreign diplomatic engagements.
articles.description: In an exclusive conversation with The Hindu, a highly-placed source says Mr. Rahman is being “misguided by his own people” on the India policy

articles.headline: French blood storage facilities impacted by recent cyber-attacks targeting medical freezers
articles.title: French blood storage impacted by freezer hacks as theories swirl about culprits
articles.summary: French authorities reported that medical facilities storing blood donations were impacted by cyber-attacks that attempted to raise cold room temperatures. The French Blood Establishment stated that staff successfully intervened to protect supplies without health impacts or product losses. Cyber-security firms are investigating potential culprits, ranging from Russian and Iranian hacktivists to organized copycats.
articles.description: The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said cold rooms storing blood were impacted by hackers.

articles.headline: Data center developers face restrictions after voters back ballot measures
articles.title: Data centers lost the midterms
articles.summary: Data center developers face a restrictive building environment after voters nationwide approved ballot measures and elected candidates favoring moratoriums on expansion. NBC News reported that 76 percent of polled voters opposed data centers in their communities. Local governments enacted measures such as a 180-day moratorium in Wells, Maine, and bans on large facilities in Ohio and Kansas, signaling a major setback for the artificial intelligence industry.
articles.description: Data center developers are poised to face a more restrictive building environment after voters across the country voted in candidates who favor moratoriums and ballot measures that put more obstacles on their expansion, delivering a stinging blow to a central pillar of the AI industry. Of voters polled by NBC News on Election Day, 76 […]

articles.headline: Uber executives report minimal transactions fulfilled by third-party AI agents
articles.title: Uber only fulfilled 4 rides from AI agents last quarter
articles.summary: Uber executives disclosed during an earnings call that third-party artificial intelligence agents accounted for only four rides and approximately 500 food deliveries during the third quarter out of 320 million total transactions. Chief Executive Officer Dara Khosrowshahi expressed openness to collaborating with third-party artificial intelligence companies while emphasizing confidence that customers will continue utilizing the direct platform application.
articles.description: AI agents won't be stealing Uber's lunch any time soon. Only four rides were arranged by third-party AI agents during the third quarter of 2026, Uber executives disclosed during an earnings call this morning. The volume of Uber Eats orders fulfilled by AI agents was a little higher, with the company recording "around 500" during […]

articles.headline: Union Cabinet approves new VISTAR scheme to overhaul national statistical architecture
articles.title: Union Cabinet approves new VISTAR scheme to overhaul India’s statistical system
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics and Research scheme with a budget of ₹4,371 crore for the period between 2026 and 2031. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation will execute the program through three components, which include conducting 59 surveys, providing funds to state governments, and undertaking the eighth Economic Census to gather granular data on unorganised sector establishments.
articles.description: The three-pronged scheme is aimed at strengthening data collecting, analysis, the incorporation of AI, as well as provide fresh data on the unorganised sector to make the overall GDP figure more accurate

articles.headline: ‘We are still red,’ Florida’s first Black governor upon win
articles.title: ‘We are still red,’ Florida’s first Black governor upon win
articles.description: US Republican Byron Donalds reiterated his support for President Donald Trump.

articles.headline: Hungary releases communist-era secret police files to the public
articles.title: Secret police files released in Hungary, 37 years after fall of communism
articles.summary: Hungary has published communist-era secret police files to help society heal from past trauma, fulfilling a pledge made by Prime Minister Péter Magyar. The digital records detail informers and handling officers, though critics warn the release is incomplete and could cause unnecessary anguish. Similar files are scheduled for digital release in February.
articles.description: Critics say the move comes too late, that the files themselves are incomplete, and the move risks sowing division and causing unnecessary anguish.

articles.headline: Mother of slain Ghanaian teenager travels to America after receiving emergency visa
articles.title: Mother of Ghanaian boy killed in US 'wants justice' as she flies for funeral
articles.summary: Doris Adu Gyamfi left Ghana for the United States after President Donald Trump granted her an emergency visa to plan the funeral of her 15-year-old son, Javits Frimpong. The teenager was fatally shot on his way to school in the Bronx on Thursday morning. Police are currently searching for three teenage suspects captured on surveillance footage while investigating the tragic shooting incident.
articles.description: Police have not made any arrests and an investigation is ongoing as authorities search for three teenage boys.

articles.headline: International Ice hockey federation maintains opposition to Russian team reinstatement
articles.title: Ice hockey federation reiterates opposition to reinstatement of Russia
articles.summary: The International Ice Hockey Federation warned of logistical and sporting challenges following a Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling to reinstate Russian teams after their exclusion following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Several national teams have refused to play against Russia, and tournament sponsor Skoda Auto stated it would reassess its involvement if Russian teams participate.
articles.description: The CAS ruled last week to overturn governing body's exclusion of ‌Russia over its 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

articles.headline: Indian Space Research Organisation successfully launches NVS-03 satellite
articles.title: Back to back GSLV successes help ISRO win back some pride
articles.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation launched the NVS-03 satellite using the GSLV-F18 vehicle from Sriharikota on October 30, 2026. The successful deployment into a geosynchronous transfer orbit provided a positive milestone for Chairman V. Narayanan following previous mission setbacks.

articles.headline: Supreme Court stays Madras High Court order on Chidambaram temple management
articles.title: Supreme Court stays Madras HC order on Chidambaram temple
articles.summary: The Supreme Court froze the implementation of an October 30 order that established a Board of Management to administer the Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple in Tamil Nadu. Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi questioned whether state high courts hold parens patriae jurisdiction over places of worship beyond public temples, while hearing arguments from the Tamil Nadu government regarding alleged maladministration and property damage.
articles.description: Questions whether High Courts have parens patriae jurisdiction only over public temples and not places of worship of other faiths

articles.headline: Death of TGSRTC conductor sparks protests across Khammam region
articles.title: TGSRTC conductor Pravalika’s death triggers protests across Khammam region; attempt-to-murder case altered to murder
articles.summary: Following the death of 24-year-old Telangana State Road Transport Corporation conductor G. Pravalika, employees staged widespread demonstrations and halted services across seven depots on November 4. Ms. Pravalika succumbed to injuries on November 3 after being pushed from a moving bus by a passenger on October 25. Police altered the initial attempt-to-murder case to murder under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

articles.headline: Kharge and Rijiju clash on social media over electoral and political issues
articles.title: Kharge asks Modi to face questions on ‘vote chori’, Rijiju spars with him on ‘dimaagi Naxals’
articles.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju clashed on the platform X on November 4 regarding the term dimaagi Naxals. Mr. Kharge urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to address allegations of vote theft and electoral roll revisions by the Election Commission. Mr. Rijiju defended the term and categorized individuals who challenge the Indian Constitution and development projects.
articles.description: The Congress president said the Election Commission had made five U-turns on the SIR, while the Union Minister defined who he called ‘dimaagi Naxals’

articles.headline: Mumbai Police arrest three individuals in connection with cyber fraud racket
articles.title: Mumbai Police arrest three in Nagpur cyber fraud racket, establish links to 73 cases across India
articles.summary: Mumbai Police arrested three men from Nagpur on November 2 for operating a share trading investment fraud racket through a shell company named Grain Garden Delight Private Limited. Authorities linked the suspects to 73 cybercrime cases nationwide after seizing various bank documents, SIM cards, and electronic items. The operation was executed by the South Region Cyber Police following a technical investigation into fraudulent financial transactions.
articles.description: The investigation began after police traced ₹24.75 lakh from a share trading investment fraud case registered at the South Region Cyber Police Station to a current account opened in the company’s name at the Central Bank of India’s Jaripatka branch in Nagpur

articles.headline: Why is the western US still counting votes after election day?
articles.title: Why is the western US still counting votes after election day?
articles.description: Why is the western US still counting votes after election day?

articles.headline: Gold prices rise as dollar index drops to five-week low
articles.title: Gold shines as dollar slips to 5-week low, investors await U.S. midterm election results
articles.summary: Spot gold prices surged 3% to reach $4,041 per ounce on November 4 as the dollar index slipped to a five-week low of 101.3. Investors awaited United States midterm election results, which indicated sweeping Democratic victories in the House and Senate. Analysts attribute the price movement to initial market reactions, with upcoming trends depending on federal policies, crude prices, and geopolitical developments.
articles.description: A weaker dollar makes dollar-denominated assets like gold less expensive for consumers of other currencies, boosting demand for the yellow metal

articles.headline: Authorities open all seventy gates of Prakasam Barrage amid heavy rainfall
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: All 70 gates of Prakasam Barrage opened; 71,000 cusecs released into Krishna
articles.summary: The Water Resources Department opened all 70 gates of the Prakasam Barrage on November 4, 2026, discharging 71,000 cusecs of surplus water into the Krishna river. Officials suspended canal supplies to prevent flooding as Cyclone Murasu brought exceptionally heavy rainfall across central districts, with Palnadu district recording nearly 269.45 millimeters of rain.
articles.description: The inflows come largely from the Keesara, Munneru and Budameru streams after heavy rain in NTR district

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh election officials review polling arrangements ahead of local body votes
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh SEC reviews cyclone impact as MPTCs, ZPTCs go to polls today
articles.summary: State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha reviewed preparations on Wednesday for MPTC and ZPTC elections across Andhra Pradesh. Despite challenges from Cyclone Murasu, district collectors reported that rainfall had subsided and voting would proceed normally. State Election Secretary A. Mallikarjuna stated that 2.52 lakh officials were deployed for duty across 31,460 polling stations to accommodate approximately 2.61 crore eligible voters.
articles.description: Around 2.61 crore voters to exercise franchise at 31,460 polling stations; decisions on polling in cyclone-hit areas will be taken based on ground-level reports, says Punetha

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces advance into al-Jawf mountain range during ongoing offensive
articles.title: Yemeni government forces claim control of strategic al-Jawf mountain range
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces advanced into the al-Dahida mountain range in eastern al-Jawf province during their ongoing offensive against Houthi forces. Troops backed by air support seized weapons and military equipment from Houthi fortifications. Meanwhile, a Houthi ballistic missile strike hit a military training camp in al-Dhalea, killing eight people and wounding over fifteen, according to a military source.
articles.description: The advance on al-Dahida heights, a strategic highland, comes as fighting escalates in al-Dhalea, Lahij and Taiz.

articles.headline: Spanish Transport Minister resigns over train crash disasters
articles.title: Spanish Transport Minister resigns over train crash disasters
articles.description: Spanish Transport Minister resigns over train crash disasters

articles.headline: Israeli settlers erect new structures on Hebron rooftops threatening Palestinian businesses
articles.title: Hebron’s Israeli rooftop settlers threaten the city’s Palestinian identity
articles.summary: Israeli settlers placed mobile structures on commercial building rooftops in Hebron on October 29 to accommodate twenty new housing units. Palestinian business owners whose shops are situated below the structures expressed deep concern over losing their livelihoods and heritage. Activists note that this expansion undermines the Palestinian identity of the Old City, which has remained heavily restricted since the 1994 Ibrahimi Mosque massacre.
articles.description: Israeli settlers have expanded in Hebron's Old City, with Palestinian residents' presence under threat.

articles.headline: European governments face persistent protests over living costs and political grievances
articles.title: Why are Europe’s governments struggling to respond to growing protests?
articles.summary: Demonstrations led largely by young people continue to sweep across at least eight European countries over grievances including school conditions, living costs, and political insecurity. Governments have struggled to respond effectively, often relying on security measures and public order responses rather than addressing underlying demands. Human rights organisations and United Nations officials have raised serious concerns regarding the use of police force against protesters.
articles.description: Protests intensify as governments prioritise security measures over addressing underlying social and economic concerns.

articles.headline: Mit Technology Review discusses data lineage for agentic enterprise security
articles.title: Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage
articles.summary: As enterprises increasingly deploy autonomous artificial intelligence agents in daily operations, organizations face significant data visibility challenges when sensitive information spreads undetected across multiple complex workflows. According to a sponsored feature by Cyberhaven published in MIT Technology Review, traditional perimeter security models are no longer sufficient. Security teams must now establish comprehensive data lineage to manage governance and accountability across hybrid human and machine systems.
articles.description: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s…

articles.headline: Tasmac staff oppose new liquor bottle buyback scheme in Tamil Nadu
articles.title: Why are Tasmac staff opposing the liquor bottle ‘buyback’ scheme in Tamil Nadu? | Explained
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation introduced a ten rupee environment cess and refund buyback scheme on November 1, 2026, prompting immediate protests and unplanned closures by outlet employees. Workers cited technical glitches in point-of-sale machines and inadequate storage space for returned bottles, following longstanding disputes over extra charges collected above the maximum retail price.
articles.description: Tasmac last week announced a ₹10 increase in the MRP of all liquor variants from November 1, 2026, by introducing an environment cess, with consumers eligible for a ₹10 refund upon returning empty bottles

articles.headline: Israeli electoral commission rejects Benjamin Netanyahu fraud allegations
articles.title: Israel election commission rejects Benjamin Netanyahu charges of fraud
articles.summary: Israeli electoral authorities rejected fraud allegations promoted by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding Arab parties after auditing 9069 polling stations on November 4, 2026. President Isaac Herzog will receive the election results to decide who forms a government, as neither Netanyahu nor rival Gadi Eisenkot secured a majority in parliament. Netanyahu faces corruption charges, while the opposition urges unity to remove him.
articles.description: The Central Elections Committee said it had conducted an audit of 9,069 polling stations following complaints and was confident that the announced results accurately reflect the will of the voters

articles.headline: Uk Supreme Court hears appeal against Palestine Action proscription
articles.title: UK Supreme Court hears appeal against Palestine Action’s proscription
articles.summary: The United Kingdom Supreme Court in London has begun a two-day hearing challenging the government designation of Palestine Action as a terrorist organization. Huda Ammori, cofounder of the direct action group, argues the ban disproportionately restricts freedom of speech. Concurrently, police arrested approximately 25 demonstrators outside the court. Rights organizations, including Amnesty International, have condemned the proscription and criticized the misuse of terrorism legislation.
articles.description: Rights activists say UK decision against Palestine Action is a 'misuse of terrorism powers'.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu launches battery energy storage systems policy to boost grid stability
articles.title: Tamil Nadu government releases three-year BESS policy
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government published a three-year storage policy on November 4, 2026, aiming to deploy 2.5 gigawatts of battery capacity. The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation will procure this capacity in the first phase. The framework mandates installations for new solar projects starting April 1, 2027, and offers transmission charge waivers to support the state's twenty-nine gigawatts of renewable energy.
articles.description: The policy aims to deploy 2.5 GW/10 GWh of Battery Energy Storage System during this period. The TNPDC will procure BESS capacity aggregating to 2,500 MW/10,000 MWh from eligible BESS projects

articles.headline: Bombay High Court advises Maharashtra to consider regulated firecracker timings
articles.title: Consider regulated timings for firecrackers, Bombay High Court tells Maharashtra government
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court suggested that the Maharashtra government and local authorities evaluate Supreme Court directives restricting Deepavali firecracker timings to curb severe pollution hazards. In a 13-page order issued on November 4, 2026, Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale also criticized the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation for selectively removing an awareness video featuring actress Dia Mirza following political objections.
articles.description: The Supreme Court had directed that the bursting of approved green crackers during Deepavali be restricted to specific windows between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. in the NCR

articles.headline: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel dies after on-field collision
articles.title: Tenerife’s Jesus de Miguel remembered in moving tributes by football world
articles.summary: Jesus de Miguel, a 30-year-old forward for Spanish football club Tenerife, died on Tuesday following a fatal on-field collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a second division match. The player suffered a cardiac arrest after being transferred to an ambulance. In response to the tragedy, the Royal Spanish Football Federation suspended domestic matches until Friday, November 6, while European football governing body UEFA announced a minute of silence for all Champions League matches.
articles.description: The 30-year-old died on Tuesday following an on-pitch collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono.

articles.headline: Sharp metal objects found in Halloween sweets across three European countries
articles.title: Sharp objects found in Halloween sweets in three European nations
articles.summary: Police issued warnings after needles, pins, screws, and nails were discovered inside Halloween sweets distributed to children in Germany, Austria, and Hungary. Authorities reported multiple injuries, including a nine-year-old girl in Germany and a ten-year-old girl in Austria. Austrian Interior Minister Gerhard Karner condemned the incidents as life-threatening, while German officials noted a significant increase in such reports compared to previous years.
articles.description: Dozens of cases are reported in Austria, Germany and Hungary, including a nine-year-old girl hurting her tongue while eating chocolate containing a pin.

articles.headline: Ravi Shankar Prasad says Punjab bears deep scars from riots and drugs
articles.title: Ravi Shankar Prasad says two blots stain Punjab’s soul: anti-Sikh riots, and drugs
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party Lok Sabha Member of Parliament Ravi Shankar Prasad stated that the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and the drug crisis remain two major wounds on Punjab that require uncompromised justice. Speaking at a conclave in Punjab on November 4, 2026, the former union minister criticized the Congress party for previously shielding key leaders and attempting to politicize the sensitive issue through public events.
articles.description: The BJP MP and former Union Minister spoke at a day-long conclave titled ‘Zakhm 84 De’ (the wounds of 1984) organised by the Punjab BJP on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots

articles.headline: Can women work in Keralam’s toddy shops? Kerala High Court answers | Explained
articles.title: Can women work in Keralam’s toddy shops? Kerala High Court answers | Explained
articles.description: Can employers legally deny women jobs in certain industries in the name of workplace safety? Does the State have the right to restrict women’s employment to protect them from possible harassment?

articles.headline: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed becomes first Muslim US Senator-elect in Michigan
articles.title: Who is Abdul El-Sayed, first Muslim U.S. Senator-elect?
articles.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's open Senate seat on Tuesday by defeating former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers. The 42-year-old former public health official secured a crucial victory that prevented Republicans from claiming the seat vacated by retiring Senator Gary Peters. El-Sayed campaigned on lowering living costs and reducing corporate influence, while overcoming unsupported Republican allegations regarding ties to the Muslim Brotherhood.
articles.description: Abdul El-Sayed is set to become the first Muslim to enter the U.S. Senate with his victory over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers in midterm elections

articles.headline: Burglars steal 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal from hockey star M.M. Somaya
articles.title: 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal stolen from home of hockey star M.M. Somaya in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Unidentified burglars stole the 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal, international sporting medals, jewellery, and cash from the Bengaluru residence of former Indian hockey captain M.M. Somaya. The theft occurred in the early hours of October 28 while the family was away in Kodagu. Indiranagar police registered a case under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and formed special teams to recover the irreplaceable national sporting honours.
articles.description: The incident, which took place in the early hours of October 28, came to light after the family returned from Kodagu district.

articles.headline: Elon Musk jokes about Republican losses following major campaign spending
articles.title: Musk makes light of defeats after record spend on Republican candidates
articles.summary: Democratic candidates secured control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives during the Tuesday elections, defeating the Republican Party across several traditional strongholds including Texas and Kansas. Technology executive Elon Musk reportedly contributed $446m to support Republican campaigns, primarily through America PAC and the Senate Leadership Fund. Following the defeats, Musk posted remarks on the social media platform X, suggesting alternative plans for artificial intelligence data centres. Democratic victor James Talarico and other successful candidates directly referenced Musk during their campaigns and victory speeches.
articles.description: Tesla and SpaceX founder Elon Musk is the world's richest man and the largest individual donor in the US midterms.

articles.headline: Sundaram Finance reports twenty-one percent profit increase in second quarter
articles.title: Sundaram Finance’s Q2 PAT up 21% to ₹475 cr.; disbursements grow 28%
articles.summary: Sundaram Finance reported a twenty-one percent year-on-year increase in standalone profit after tax to four hundred seventy-five crore rupees for the second quarter of financial year twenty-seven. Chennai-based non-banking financial company disbursements rose twenty-eight percent to ten thousand three hundred fifty-five crore rupees, supported by strong domestic economic momentum, improved asset quality, and expanding assets under management.
articles.description: Chennai-based NBFC reports 19% growth in assets under management to ₹65,992 crore; net Stage 3 assets improve to 0.91% as of September-end

articles.headline: Canva restructures its workforce amidst the rapid growth of generative AI
articles.title: As Canva restructures, how is AI reshaping creative businesses? | Explained
articles.summary: Design platform Canva announced plans to reorganise its staff due to slowing growth and technological shifts. The company is navigating changes as generative AI reshapes creative businesses by altering how visual content is produced and sold. Other firms in the creative industry are similarly addressing the opportunities and challenges introduced by artificial intelligence across global markets.
articles.description: Canva says 1,271 jobs are affected by its reorganisation amid slowing growth. Adobe, Figma and Getty Images show how generative AI is reshaping products, costs and business models in the creative industry

articles.headline: Kerala draft report proposes higher minimum wages and bonus eligibility
articles.title: Draft report on implementation of Labour Codes moots higher minimum wages, wider eligibility for bonus
articles.summary: A newly submitted draft report on implementing four Labour Codes recommends expanding worker family units and increasing minimum wage calculations. Submitted to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on November 4, 2026, the panel also proposes mandatory free medical check-ups for hazardous occupations and enhanced safety provisions for female night-shift workers across the state.
articles.description: The draft report was submitted by Minister for Labour Bindhu Krishna to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday.

articles.headline: Can women work in Keralam’s toddy shops? Kerala High Court answers | Explained
articles.title: Can women work in Keralam’s toddy shops? Kerala High Court answers | Explained
articles.description: Can employers legally deny women jobs in certain industries in the name of workplace safety? Does the State have the right to restrict women’s employment to protect them from possible harassment?

articles.headline: Thailand requires formal Chinese extradition request for detained Uyghur men
articles.title: China must make extradition request if it wants two Uyghur men returned: Thailand
articles.summary: National Security Council head Chaipruak Doungprapat stated that China must file a formal extradition request to deport two detained Uyghur men. While human rights advocates express fears of torture if returned, the judicial process will determine their fate following letters pleading against deportation from the Suan Plu immigration detention centre in Bangkok.
articles.description: The two men, in letters shared last week, pleaded not to be sent back to China

articles.headline: Supreme Court stays Madras High Court order on Chidambaram temple administration
articles.title: SC stays Madras HC order on Chidambaram temple
articles.summary: The Supreme Court froze a Madras High Court order that formed a Board of Management to administer the ancient Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple in Tamil Nadu. Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi questioned state high court jurisdiction over public temples during the November 4, 2026 hearing after challenges from the Podhu Dikshidar hereditary priests.
articles.description: Questions whether High Courts have parens patriae jurisdiction only over public temples and not places of worship of other faiths

articles.headline: India records below average monsoon despite shaping El Nino
articles.title: Why even a strong El Niño does not guarantee a poor Indian monsoon
articles.summary: The 2026 southwest monsoon concluded nearly thirteen percent below the long term average of eighty seven centimeters, accompanied by a developing El Nino expected to peak in December. East and Northeast India experienced their driest season since records began in 1901. Historically, strong El Nino events do not always guarantee poor monsoon outcomes.
articles.description: Seven Indian monsoons since 1950 have run into a moderate or strong El Niño. Of these, in five years, including 2026, monsoon rainfall levels were at least 10% lower than the long-term average. The IMD refers to this level as 'deficient’. The 2023 season was something of an exception with ‘below average’ rainfall. However, 1997 had ‘average’ rainfall

articles.headline: South Africa holds local elections amid declining support for African National Congress
articles.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
articles.summary: South Africans voted in local elections on November 4, 2026, with polls indicating a substantial decline in support for the ruling African National Congress due to widespread public frustration over unemployment, crime, and deteriorating basic service delivery across municipalities. The African National Congress previously lost its parliamentary majority. Analysts predict the party will record its worst electoral performance as competing political entities vie to govern nearly 300 municipal regions.
articles.description: As South Africans vote in local elections, residents tell the BBC they are tired of the poor quality of services they get.

articles.headline: NBA confirms removal of Rwandan army team over US sanctions
articles.title: Rwanda's army team removed from Africa league after US sanctions, NBA says
articles.summary: The National Basketball Association confirmed it removed Rwanda's army-funded Armée Patriotique Rwandaise club from the Basketball Africa League due to United States sanctions imposed in March. Responding to a congressional inquiry on October 23, 2026, league officials stated the team will remain barred while sanctions against Rwanda's military and defense ministry for activities in the Democratic Republic of Congo stay in place.
articles.description: The US imposed sanctions on Rwanda's army over its role in the conflict in DR Congo.

articles.headline: Union Cabinet approves 14,500 crore rupees funding scheme for energy storage systems
articles.title: Cabinet clears ₹14,500 crore viability gap funding scheme for 92 GWh battery energy storage systems
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved fourteen thousand five hundred crore rupees in viability gap funding on Wednesday for grid-scale energy storage systems spanning financial year 2027 through financial year 2031. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated in New Delhi that the initiative supports ninety-two gigawatt-hours of storage capacity across three technologies to help India achieve its target of five hundred gigawatts of renewable energy by 2030.
articles.description: The scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh storage capacity across three technologies — Battery Energy Storage System (30 GWh), Pumped Storage Projects (60 GWh) and Emerging Storage Technologies (2GW)

articles.headline: Modi and Naidu review cyclone devastation in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Modi calls Naidu, reviews damage from Cyclones Arnab and Murasu
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on November 4, 2026, to review recovery efforts following Cyclones Arnab and Murasu. Naidu reported severe damage to agriculture, roads, and power infrastructure, requesting ₹4,563 crore in immediate aid for Cyclone Arnab alone, while preliminary assessments place Cyclone Murasu damages at ₹343 crore according to the Chief Minister’s Office.
articles.description: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister seeks Central assistance for losses suffered by farmers and damage to roads and power lines

articles.headline: P.V. Sindhu discusses rebuilding career after winning Hylo Open
articles.title: With two titles in 4 months, P.V. Sindhu says she is building, not chasing her old self
articles.summary: Indian badminton player P.V. Sindhu secured her second title in four months at the Hylo Open on November 1, 2026, returning to world number six. The thirty-one-year-old attributed her resurgence to a revamped support team, including her husband. She emphasised proper rest, recovery, and preparation for the upcoming fifteen-point scoring format changes while praising emerging female players.
articles.description: The switch to a 15-point scoring format from next year will demand another adjustment, and Sindhu believes players will have less time to recover from a slow start

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate raids former APPSC secretary over recruitment irregularities
articles.title: ED searches IPS officer Sitarama Anjaneyulu, others in APPSC Group-I evaluation case
articles.summary: Enforcement Directorate officials conducted searches across seven locations in Hyderabad, Secunderabad, and Guntur district on November 4, 2026. The raids targeted former Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission secretary P. Sitarama Anjaneyulu and CamSign Media owner P. Madhusudhan Rao regarding alleged manual evaluation irregularities in the 2020 Group-I recruitment examination following a Prevention of Money Laundering Act case registration.
articles.description: ED officials search the houses of retired IPS officer P. Sitarama Anjaneyulu and CamSign Media owner P. Madhusudhan Rao and the Haailand resort in Guntur district

articles.headline: Indian-origin candidates contest across United States midterm elections
articles.title: Who are the Indian-origin candidates in U.S. midterm elections?
articles.summary: Numerous individuals with South Asian heritage are running for public office in the November 2026 legislative contests across various American states. Prominent incumbent lawmakers and new nominees are seeking positions in Congress, state executive offices, and local governments. These campaigns encompass multiple jurisdictions, highlighting the growing political participation of this community within the American electoral system.
articles.description: Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress

articles.headline: Indian sailor killed in suspected drone attack off Oman coast
articles.title: Attack on vessel near Hormuz Strait: Deceased sailor hailed from Gujarat, kin plan burial in Oman
articles.summary: A twenty-five-year-old sailor from Gujarat named Nahim Ajij Gandhar died following a suspected drone attack on an Indian-flagged cargo vessel near the Strait of Oman on November 2, 2026. Thirteen other crew members survived and were rescued by the Omani Coast Guard. The vessel and its date consignment were destroyed, prompting India to urge diplomatic solutions and safe passage corridors.
articles.description: Nahim Ajij Gandhar was among the 14 crew members on board the vessel, which was registered at Bedi port in Gujarat’s Jamnagar district

articles.headline: INCOIS issues marine heat wave and swell surge warnings for India
articles.title: INCOIS warns of Marine Heat Wave, issues swell surge alert for east and west coasts
articles.summary: The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services issued a marine heat wave warning across the Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean, and Bay of Bengal on November 4, 2026. Additionally, officials issued a swell surge warning for both the east and west coasts, including the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where waves exceeding one metre are expected to impact coastal ecosystems.
articles.description: The warming conditions could adversely affect coral reef ecosystems, marine productivity and coastal biodiversity

articles.headline: Can Russia compete with the US, China and the EU in Africa?
articles.title: Can Russia compete with the US, China and the EU in Africa?
articles.description: Moscow pledges more trade and investment in Africa, where leaders want local industries, technology and jobs.

articles.headline: India opts to bowl first in opening ODI against New Zealand
articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st ODI: Pacers, Kohli script impressive win for India
articles.summary: India captain Shubman Gill elected to field first against New Zealand in the opening One Day International in Auckland on November 4, 2026. The visiting team deployed four specialist fast bowlers alongside spin-bowling all-rounder Naman Dhir. New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner leads the hosts in the match, which features a confirmed lineup including veteran batsmen Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma.
articles.description: India reached the revised target of 143 in 22.4 overs of the rain-curtalied match with Kohli’s 51-ball knock doing bulk of the damage

articles.headline: Ugandan critics face abductions and legal charges over online posts
articles.title: ‘I will not delete my posts’: Inside Uganda’s crackdown on online critics
articles.summary: Ugandan authorities have detained citizens and critics, including Praise Aloikin Opoloje and journalist Andrew Tabandama Natumanya, over social media posts and reporting criticizing powerful figures such as President Yoweri Museveni and military chief General Muhoozi Kainerugaba. Victims allege they were abducted by armed men in Toyota HiAce vans, assaulted, and threatened before facing formal court charges or brief detentions. The crackdown highlights ongoing risks for individuals using digital platforms to challenge the government in Kampala.
articles.description: Uganda’s online critics allege abductions and intimidation as families search for missing relatives.

articles.headline: South Korean appeals court upholds former President Yoon Suk Yeol conviction
articles.title: Seoul court upholds ex-President Yoon’s election conviction
articles.summary: A South Korean appeals court on Wednesday upheld former President Yoon Suk Yeol’s 18-month suspended sentence for spreading disinformation during his campaign. The ruling affirms a lower court verdict regarding false statements about his ties to a shaman. If the Supreme Court upholds the decision, Yoon's 2022 election victory could be invalidated and his former party, the People Power Party, would be forced to repay nearly thirty million dollars in campaign expenses.
articles.description: The ruling affirmed a lower court verdict that found Mr. Yoon guilty of violating election laws by making false statements during his campaign, including lying about his ties to a shaman

articles.headline: Who holds the power today? Governments or corporations?
articles.title: Who holds the power today? Governments or corporations?
articles.description: Who holds the power today? Governments or corporations?

articles.headline: Transport corporation employees protest after injured Telangana bus conductor dies.
articles.title: Telangana bus conductor Pravalika, who was pushed off moving bus, dies; she took up RTC job after father’s death
articles.summary: Telangana State Road Transport Corporation employees staged widespread demonstrations across Khammam after twenty-four-year-old conductor G. Pravalika succumbed to injuries sustained on October 25. The employee had been allegedly pushed from a moving bus by a passenger during a ticket dispute. Police altered the charges against the arrested suspect following the worker's death, prompting transport workers to demand stricter safety measures.
articles.description: Her death sparks outrage. TGSRTC staff protest across Khammam region.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh water resources minister puts officials on alert for cyclone rainfall.
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: Ramanaidu puts irrigation officials on high alert over swollen rivers, drains
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Minister Nimmala Ramanaidu ordered irrigation officials to maintain high vigilance on Wednesday due to heavy downpours from Cyclone Murasu. The minister instructed authorities to drain stagnant agricultural water, monitor rising river levels, and manage flood flows across multiple districts. Officials were further directed to ensure coordinated emergency responses to protect crops and public safety.
articles.description: The Nallamada and Parchur drains are flowing above their maximum levels around Parchur, Bapatla and Chirala
